question: If your accelerator becomes stuck while driving, what should you do first?
options: a:Shift to neutral and apply steady pressure on the brake.,b:Reach down and try to pull the pedal up.,c:Shift into park immediately.
note: Keep control, shift to neutral, brake steadily, and then pull off the road safely before turning off the engine.

question: After a suspended license is restored, how long is the probationary driving period?
options: a:Two years.,b:One year.,c:Six months.
note: Drivers whose privileges were suspended and later restored are placed on probation for one year; violations during this time may result in further suspension.

question: When changing lanes you should:
options: a:Rely only on your mirrors.,b:Begin signaling as you move into the lane.,c:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes and check blind spots.
note: Signal before you change lanes (about 100 feet in residential areas), check mirrors and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots.

question: How should you scan the road to prepare for hazards ahead?
options: a:Fix your gaze straight ahead at all times.,b:Keep your left foot lightly on the brake pedal.,c:Continuously scan the entire roadway and adjacent areas.
note: Search well ahead, to the sides, and behind to identify potential problems before they occur. Constant scanning helps you react early.

question: What is the best way to avoid hydroplaning on wet roads?
options: a:Speed up to get through puddles quickly.,b:Use cruise control at all times.,c:Drive in the center of the roadway only.,d:Maintain properly inflated and treaded tires and reduce speed on wet surfaces.
note: Proper tire maintenance and reducing speed in wet conditions help prevent hydroplaning and loss of control.

question: When backing your vehicle, what is the correct practice?
options: a:Turn your head and look out the rear window rather than relying solely on mirrors.,b:Rely only on your mirrors.,c:Open the driver's door to see if it is safe.
note: When reversing, look over your shoulder and check behind your vehicle; do not depend only on mirrors or sensors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a green light, you must do which of the following?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians and any vehicles with the right-of-way.,b:Maintain your normal speed and proceed.,c:Stop and search for nearby police cars first.
note: Unless a sign prohibits it, you may turn on green but must yield to pedestrians and any oncoming traffic that has the right-of-way.

question: When faced with an oncoming car on the left and a bicyclist on the right, what is the safest move?
options: a:Let the oncoming car pass first, then pass the bicyclist.,b:Drive between them and split the difference.,c:Pull onto the shoulder to pass both at once.
note: Deal with one hazard at a time: let the oncoming car pass, then safely pass the bicyclist when clear.

question: A regulatory sign showing a red circle with a slash through a black symbol means:
options: a:Drivers should come to a complete stop.,b:The depicted action is forbidden.,c:Some drivers should yield to others.
note: A red circle with a diagonal slash identifies actions that are prohibited, such as no U-turn or no left turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane should you begin a left turn from multilane one-way streets or highways?
options: a:The far left lane.,b:The right lane.,c:The middle of the intersection.
note: When turning left from a multi-lane one-way street or highway, start from the left-most lane designated for left turns.

question: A solid yellow arrow in a turn signal indicates:
options: a:Drivers may turn in the arrow direction without caution.,b:It has the same meaning as a circular yellow light.,c:It is not used in traffic signals.
note: A solid yellow arrow warns drivers that the protected turn is ending and they should prepare to stop or yield to others.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it appropriate to signal?
options: a:Never—signaling is optional.,b:Only when turning right.,c:When changing lanes, pulling into/out of parking, or entering traffic from an alley or parking space.,d:Only when turning left.
note: Always signal before you change lanes, enter traffic from a parking area, or make turns so other road users know your intentions.

question: On a long trip, what is a good practice to relieve driver fatigue?
options: a:Stop and rest every two hours for a short break.,b:Drive with one eye open at a time.,c:Do arm exercises while driving every hour.
note: To avoid fatigue, stop periodically—about every two hours—for a short break, nap, or rest.

question: What is the “No zone” in relation to large trucks and buses?
options: a:A restricted lane for large vehicles only.,b:The large blind spots around a truck or bus where smaller vehicles disappear from view.,c:A special speed limit area near heavy vehicles.
note: Trucks and buses have significant blind spots on each side, in front, and behind; avoid lingering in these “No zones.”

question: Anything that forces you to do which action could cause a crash?
options: a:Take your eyes off the road.,b:Take your hands off the wheel.,c:Take your attention away from driving.
note: Distractions that take your attention from driving, your eyes off the road, or hands off the wheel increase crash risk.

question: Which driving behavior is a telltale sign of a drunk driver?
options: a:Driving somewhat more slowly than surrounding traffic only.,b:Weaving between lanes.,c:Always driving in a perfectly straight line.
note: Signs of impairment include weaving, sudden speed changes, jerky driving, and unexpected stops or swerves.

question: What is the best method to handle a tailgater?
options: a:Change lanes or gradually slow to encourage them to pass.,b:Slam on your brakes to warn them.,c:Speed up to put distance between you and the tailgater.
note: If someone follows too closely, signal and change lanes when safe, or gradually slow to allow them to pass to reduce rear-end collision risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you're not in the correct lane to make a turn at an intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Drive on to the next intersection and make the turn from the proper lane.,b:Quickly cut across traffic to make the turn.,c:Turn from your current lane after signaling.
note: Avoid last-minute lane changes or turns; proceed to the next intersection and turn from the correct lane.

question: Which factor most affects your ability to stop?
options: a:Road and weather conditions.,b:The state of traffic lights.,c:The time of day.
note: Stopping distance is greatly affected by road surface and weather; reduce speed when conditions are poor to maintain control.

question: On a snow-covered road, maintain a following distance of at least:
options: a:Three seconds.,b:Six seconds.,c:Nine seconds.
note: Increase your following distance in slippery conditions; on snow-covered roads a minimum of six seconds is recommended.

question: A round road sign typically indicates:
options: a:An upcoming railroad crossing.,b:A no passing zone.,c:A school zone.
note: Round traffic signs are used to warn drivers that they are approaching a railroad crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended downward, what is the hand signal indicating?
options: a:The driver intends to stop or slow down.,b:The driver intends to turn left.,c:The driver intends to turn right.
note: An arm extended downward from the left side signals that the driver plans to stop or slow down.

question: A flashing red traffic signal means the same as which of the following?
options: a:Yield sign.,b:Stop sign.,c:Solid green light.,d:Pedestrian crosswalk signal.
note: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign: stop completely, then proceed when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the right.,b:The driver on the left.,c:The driver that signals first.
note: When two vehicles arrive at an open intersection simultaneously, yield to the vehicle on your right; then proceed when safe.

question: What should you do when you see a school crossing sign?
options: a:Always stop even if there is no stop sign.,b:Always sound your horn when children are present.,c:Watch for children, slow down, and be ready to stop.
note: Be alert for children near school crossings and be prepared to stop; obey crossing guards and posted speeds.

question: A five-ounce glass of wine contains about the same alcohol as which drink?
options: a:A 12-ounce can or bottle of beer.,b:One pint of whiskey.,c:A gallon of wine.
note: A 5-ounce glass of wine (about 12% alcohol) has roughly the same alcohol content as a 12-ounce beer or 1.5 ounces of 86-proof liquor.

question: Which behavior can indicate an aggressive driver?
options: a:Maintaining a three-second following distance.,b:Failing to properly yield the right-of-way.,c:Never changing lanes.
note: Aggressive drivers may make erratic lane changes, follow too closely, or fail to yield; avoid confronting them and give them space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is a correct practice when passing another vehicle?
options: a:Use only your mirrors; checking over your shoulder is unnecessary.,b:When passing, wait until you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview before returning.,c:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes and ensure no oncoming traffic.
note: When passing, always signal in advance, check mirrors and blind spots, and only return to your lane when you can see the passed vehicle's front in your rearview.

question: If a school bus is stopped in front of a school to drop off passengers, you may pass it at no more than:
options: a:15 mph.,b:25 mph.,c:10 mph.
note: When a school bus is stopped at a school for loading or unloading, other vehicles may pass at no more than 10 mph and only if it is safe.

question: How is drinking and driving classified in terms of traffic safety?
options: a:A minor traffic safety problem.,b:A serious traffic safety problem.,c:Safe if you have only had a few drinks.
note: Driving while impaired by alcohol or drugs is a serious safety issue — it greatly increases the risk of crashes and injuries.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching an intersection with a steady green light, what is the proper approach?
options: a:Proceed, but yield to vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection and be prepared to stop.,b:Always stop briefly before going.,c:Treat it like a four-way stop.
note: You may continue through a steady green but must yield to any pedestrians or vehicles already in the intersection and be prepared to stop if the light changes.

question: What lighting is recommended when driving in rain?
options: a:Use low beam headlights.,b:Use high beam headlights.,c:Use parking lights.
note: In rainy conditions, low beam headlights increase your visibility to others; high beams can reduce visibility by reflecting off rain.

question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, what should you do?
options: a:Get out of the car and walk for help.,b:Lie down in the car and go to sleep.,c:Stay inside the vehicle and wait for help.
note: If stranded in a snowstorm stay in your vehicle, conserve warmth, and wait for help. Leaving the vehicle can make you harder to find and more exposed to danger.

question: If another driver cuts you off, the best response is to:
options: a:Pull next to them and argue.,b:Let it go and continue driving safely.,c:Flash your lights aggressively.
note: Avoid road rage: stay calm, do not retaliate, and move safely out of the way when possible.

question: Compared to daytime driving, driving at night is typically:
options: a:More dangerous due to reduced visibility and other factors.,b:Less dangerous.,c:No different in risk level.
note: Night driving is more hazardous because visibility is reduced and glare and impaired drivers may be present.

question: What helps reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Not speeding in wet conditions.,b:Replacing tires only when punctured.,c:Lowering tire pressure below the recommended level.
note: To lower hydroplaning risk, drive slower in rain, maintain proper tire pressure, and replace tires with worn tread.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing and you do not see or hear a train, you must stop if:
options: a:A crossing gate is lowered.,b:A stop sign is posted.,c:The crossing lights are flashing.
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing when flashing red lights are activated, a gate is lowered, a stop sign is posted, a flagger directs you, or a train is visible or too close to safely cross.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are waiting to make a left turn at a multilane intersection and cannot see because opposing traffic blocks your view, what should you do?
options: a:Wait until you can see all lanes you must cross before starting the turn.,b:Accelerate quickly when the first lane is clear.,c:Proceed if an oncoming driver waves you on.
note: Never begin a left turn until you can see that all lanes you must cross are clear and you can complete the turn safely.

question: Which statement about passing motorcycles is correct?
options: a:You must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle.,b:Motorcycles are entitled to the full width of a lane and you must ensure your vehicle is entirely in the left lane before passing.,c:You may follow motorcycles closely.,d:Motorcycles are always slower than cars so you can pass without checking.
note: Motorcycles occupy a full lane; be sure your vehicle is fully in the adjacent lane before passing and give ample space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a turn, what should you normally do with your speed?
options: a:Reduce your speed so you can maintain control of the vehicle.,b:Increase your speed to complete the turn quickly.,c:Maintain the same speed as before the turn.
note: Slow to a safe speed for turning so you can stay in your lane and respond to hazards.

question: A single broken yellow line down the center of a two-lane road means:
options: a:Lanes move in the same direction and passing is not allowed.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.,c:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is never allowed.
note: A broken yellow centerline separates opposing traffic and means passing is permitted if it is safe to do so.

question: The effect alcohol has on reflexes and judgement depends on what?
options: a:Whether you are drinking hard cider rather than mixed drinks.,b:How much alcohol is in the bloodstream, not the type of drink.,c:Whether you drink beer instead of wine.
note: Any type of alcohol impairs reflexes and judgment equally for the same BAC; the effect depends on how much alcohol is in the blood.

question: Drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving:
options: a:Are always aware of the risks they are taking.,b:Do not have sufficient control over their bodies, minds, or the vehicle being driven.,c:Are better drivers because they are more careful than sober drivers.
note: Alcohol impairs judgment, coordination, reaction time, and decision-making, reducing a driver's ability to operate a vehicle safely.

question: If you begin to feel tired while driving, the safest action is to:
options: a:Get some coffee and keep driving.,b:Open your window and continue.,c:Stop driving and rest.
note: Drowsy driving reduces reaction time and decision-making; the safest response is to stop driving and rest.

question: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across lanes to show where drivers must stop at:
options: a:Curves and hills.,b:Church and school entrances.,c:Driveways only.,d:Intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
note: Stop lines indicate the exact location where you must stop at intersections and marked crosswalks.

question: If another person is injured in an accident, what should you do regarding their care?
options: a:Do not move the injured unnecessarily; keep them warm and administer first aid as you can.,b:Move the injured immediately to safer ground.,c:Always leave the injured where they lie without touching them.
note: Avoid moving injured people unless there is immediate danger; keep them warm and provide first aid while waiting for professional help.

question: Which of these statements about changing weather is true?
options: a:A sudden change in weather requires you to adjust your driving.,b:You should always drive at the posted speed in rain and fog.,c:Ignore vehicles behind you in poor weather.
note: When weather changes, reduce speed and increase caution; adjust following distances and driving behavior to match conditions.

question: Which of the following can cause distracted driving?
options: a:Eating, drinking, smoking, texting, or changing the radio.,b:Only talking to a passenger.,c:Only checking mirrors occasionally.
note: Any secondary activity—eating, texting, adjusting devices—can distract you from driving and increase crash risk.

question: A traffic signal showing a green arrow with a red light means:
options: a:You may only drive straight ahead.,b:You may proceed only in the direction of the green arrow.,c:You must wait for a solid green light to go in any direction.
note: When a green arrow is displayed you may go only in the direction the arrow points, even if other signal aspects are red.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to pass another vehicle on the right?
options: a:Even if it means driving off the pavement.,b:If the other vehicle is waiting to turn left and an available lane exists to the right.,c:On a narrow bridge.
note: You may pass on the right when there is a sufficient lane to do so safely or when the vehicle ahead is turning left and you can pass without leaving the paved roadway.

question: Drivers may not pass from either side across what centerline?
options: a:A single broken yellow line.,b:A combination solid and broken yellow line.,c:Double solid yellow lines.
note: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing from either direction, except for permitted left turns.

question: What does a slow-moving vehicle emblem indicate?
options: a:The vehicle is an emergency vehicle.,b:The vehicle is a commercial truck.,c:The vehicle must always pull over.,d:The vehicle is moving 25 mph or slower.
note: A reflective orange triangle signifies a slow-moving vehicle likely traveling 25 mph or less—be prepared to slow.

question: If your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down, steer parallel to the road, then ease back onto the pavement when safe.,b:Stop immediately on the shoulder.,c:Accelerate and steer sharply back onto the road.
note: If right wheels leave the pavement, ease off the gas, keep steering straight, slow down, and carefully ease back onto the roadway when safe.

question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic accidents?
options: a:Inattentive driving, excessive speed for conditions, and following too closely.,b:Only faulty vehicles.,c:Perfect weather conditions.,d:Driving the speed limit.
note: Inattentive driving, driving too fast for conditions, and tailgating are common causes of crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Only if there is no oncoming traffic.,b:Yes.,c:No.
note: Double solid yellow centerlines separate opposing traffic and passing across them is prohibited except to make a left turn into or from a driveway, alley, or private road.

question: If you are involved in an accident, what is your first responsibility at the scene?
options: a:Stop immediately at the scene.,b:Call the police first.,c:Help injured persons before stopping.
note: You must stop immediately. If safe, move the vehicle out of traffic, call the police, and render aid as appropriate.

question: Which of the following can lead to impairment and potentially a DUII?
options: a:Beer, wine, and other alcoholic beverages.,b:Controlled substances and prescription medicines that impair driving.,c:Inhalants such as glue or paint.,d:All of the above.
note: Many substances—alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and some prescription or over-the-counter medications—can impair driving and result in DUII charges.

question: Is it legal to drink alcoholic beverages while in a vehicle on a public highway?
options: a:No,b:Yes,c:You yes
note: It is illegal to consume or have an open alcoholic beverage in areas of a vehicle normally occupied by driver or passenger on public roads in New Jersey.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn the front wheels sharply toward the curb.,b:Turn the wheels slightly to the right.,c:Turn the front wheels sharply away from the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels sharply away from the curb so that if the vehicle rolls, it will roll away from traffic and into the curb.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is passing prohibited?
options: a:On hills or curves and at intersections, and in other no-passing zones.,b:Only when a school bus has its red lights flashing.,c:Only on highways with median barriers.
note: Do not pass on hills, curves, intersections, railroad crossings, bridges, or any no-passing zone.

question: What is the effect of taking drugs together with alcohol?
options: a:It increases the risk of causing a crash.,b:It is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.,c:It lessens the effect of alcohol on driving ability.
note: Combining drugs with alcohol can compound impairment and significantly increase crash risk.

question: A 'Reduced speed, 35 mph' sign means what?
options: a:The new posted speed limit of 35 mph begins at that sign.,b:The reduced speed begins at the next sign.,c:You have lots of time to slow down after the sign.,d:The advisory speed applies only to trucks.
note: A posted reduced speed sign indicates the new posted limit begins where the sign is located.

question: A flashing red traffic light corresponds to which action at the intersection?
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield to cross traffic/pedestrians, and proceed when the way is clear.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution without stopping.,c:Continue normally through the intersection if it is clear.
note: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign: stop, yield, and proceed only when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you approach an intersection showing a flashing red light, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop, then go when it is clear.,c:Proceed without stopping if no other vehicles are present.,d:Turn around and find another route.
note: A flashing red light requires a full stop; only proceed when the intersection is clear and it is safe to go.

question: To check your blind spot when changing lanes to the left you should glance:
options: a:Over your right shoulder.,b:At your side mirror.,c:Over your left shoulder.
note: Turn your head and glance over the shoulder in the direction you plan to move to verify there are no vehicles in the blind spot.

question: What should you do before changing lanes on a multilane highway?
options: a:Sound your horn.,b:Turn on your headlights.,c:Check mirrors and glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot.
note: Before changing lanes, check your rearview and side mirrors and then glance over your shoulder to ensure no one is in your blind spot.

question: Approximately how far might a fully loaded tractor-trailer take to stop from 55 mph?
options: a:50 feet.,b:125 feet.,c:400 feet.,d:200 feet.
note: Large, fully loaded tractor-trailers may require up to about 400 feet to come to a complete stop from 55 mph.

question: What is the only effective way to reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Drink coffee.,b:Exercise.,c:Allow your body time to metabolize the alcohol.
note: Time is the only proven way to lower BAC; coffee, rest, or exercise do not reduce the alcohol in your bloodstream.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A red traffic signal requires you to:
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection.,b:Stop only if other vehicles are present.,c:Slow down and proceed carefully without stopping.
note: Stop at the stop line, or before any crosswalk or intersection, and remain stopped while the light is red.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct way to merge onto a highway from an entrance ramp?
options: a:Enter well above the speed of traffic to get ahead.,b:Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.,c:Use the acceleration lane to reach highway speed and merge into traffic.
note: Use the ramp's acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic, signal, look for an opening, and merge safely into the flow.

question: When applying the crash-prevention formula, what should a driver do?
options: a:Be alert, be prepared, and act in time.,b:Drive only in daylight.,c:Always stay below the speed limit.,d:Ignore other drivers.
note: To avoid crashes, drivers should be alert to hazards, prepared for possible actions, and act in time to prevent collisions.

question: What is the safest way to pass a bicyclist on a two-lane road without bicycle lanes?
options: a:Slow down until no traffic is approaching, then pass leaving sufficient space.,b:Continue straight because the bicyclist must get out of the way.,c:Do not pass until you reach a traffic signal or stop sign.
note: Pass bicyclists as you would other vehicles but allow at least 3 feet of clearance (more on higher-speed roads) and avoid honking unnecessarily.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic signal turns green, what must you do before proceeding?
options: a:Accelerate immediately to clear the intersection quickly.,b:Sound your horn and go.,c:Back up to check traffic behind you.,d:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.
note: A green light permits movement, but you must first yield to pedestrians and any traffic still in the intersection.

question: When approaching railroad tracks you should:
options: a:Speed up to clear the tracks quickly.,b:Look, listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop.,c:Try to drive around lowered gates.
note: Approach railroad crossings with caution: look both ways, listen for trains, and be prepared to stop if signals or gates are activated.

question: How should drivers respond to a steady red traffic light?
options: a:Stop completely before the intersection.,b:Proceed if no other traffic is present.,c:Continue driving unless a police officer is present.
note: A steady red light requires a full stop. Turning on red is allowed only where not prohibited and only after yielding to traffic and pedestrians.

question: Who should wear seat belts for maximum protection?
options: a:Only the person driving the car.,b:Passengers only on long drives.,c:All occupants of the vehicle.
note: All occupants should wear seat belts on every trip; unbelted passengers can be thrown and injure others in a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign, what action is required?
options: a:Yield only to traffic on the right.,b:Always come to a complete stop even if clear.,c:Slow down and yield the right-of-way to traffic in the street you are entering.
note: A yield sign means slow down and give way to vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection or roadway.

question: A person using a white cane or guide dog is most likely to be which of the following?
options: a:A blind person.,b:A traffic study participant.,c:A deaf person.,d:A bicyclist.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog, as they are likely blind and need extra consideration.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a freeway, you should:
options: a:Drive slowly on the ramp to better check traffic.,b:Signal and expect freeway traffic to yield to you.,c:Signal, yield to existing traffic, and enter at approximately the same speed traffic is moving.
note: When merging, match the speed of traffic and yield to vehicles already on the freeway to merge safely.

question: Which practices help you stay alert while driving on major highways?
options: a:Stay alert, keep your eyes moving, and be ready to react to hazards.,b:Stare at the center line to avoid distractions.,c:Rely on cruise control without watching the road.,d:Listen to loud music the entire trip.
note: Avoid highway hypnosis by keeping your eyes moving, scanning the road, and staying prepared to react to unexpected hazards.

question: When an emergency vehicle using sirens and lights approaches you, you must immediately:
options: a:Pull to the right side of the road and stop.,b:Pull to the right and slow down only.,c:Turn on your four-way flashers while continuing.
note: Immediately drive to the right and stop so the emergency vehicle can pass; remain stopped until it has passed.

question: How should drivers treat traffic signs and pavement markings?
options: a:They must always obey them.,b:They are only suggestions.,c:They apply only when there is other traffic.
note: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control flow and safety; you are required to obey them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When do you have the right-of-way when turning left with traffic control?
options: a:When a green arrow points left.,b:When the light is a solid green without arrow.,c:When a flashing yellow light is on.
note: A steady green arrow pointing left gives you the right-of-way to turn left while oncoming traffic is stopped by the signal.

question: What can happen if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?
options: a:The medicine will reduce the effect of alcohol.,b:Alcohol will improve the medicine's effectiveness.,c:The combination may multiply the effects of both the alcohol and the medicine.
note: Combining alcohol with medications can increase impairment and produce stronger effects than either substance alone.

question: Regulatory signs are usually what color and must always be obeyed?
options: a:Blue,b:White,c:Green
note: Regulatory signs control traffic movement and are typically white with black markings; they must be obeyed by motorists.

question: What documents must you present to obtain a New Jersey driver license or non-driver ID?
options: a:Proof of age, identity, and legal U.S. presence (plus address and SSN).,b:Only proof of residency.,c:A utility bill only.,d:No documents are required.
note: Applicants must provide documents proving age, identity, legal presence, residence, and their Social Security number (or an SSA exemption).

question: When a traffic signal shows a steady green arrow, drivers should:
options: a:Turn in the arrow's direction after yielding to vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection.,b:Merge into the lane indicated by the arrow.,c:Slow to a stop, if it is safe to do so.
note: A steady green arrow permits you to turn in the direction of the arrow, but you must be in the proper lane and yield to vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a street from a driveway, what must you do?
options: a:Drive slowly so approaching vehicles and pedestrians can get out of your way.,b:Sound your horn to warn pedestrians and drivers.,c:Stop and proceed only when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
note: Always stop before entering the roadway from a driveway, yield to pedestrians and vehicles, and do not cross the sidewalk area until it is safe.

question: As a pedestrian, what is the safest practice when crossing?
options: a:Never enter a crosswalk when vehicles are approaching closely.,b:Always insist on the right-of-way over vehicles.,c:Enter crosswalks at any time, since vehicles must stop.,d:Cross while looking at your phone.
note: Even though pedestrians have rights, do not step into a crosswalk if vehicles are too close to safely stop.

question: What do crossbuck signs warn drivers of?
options: a:Railroad crossings ahead.,b:School zones.,c:No passing zones.
note: A crossbuck marks a railroad crossing. Approach with caution and yield to any approaching trains.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving in traffic, what is the safest general strategy regarding speed?
options: a:Drive at roughly the same speed as the flow of traffic within posted limits.,b:Drive faster than the flow to get through quickly.,c:Drive noticeably slower than the flow to be cautious.
note: Driving at the flow of traffic (within the speed limit) reduces the chance of collisions caused by speed differentials.

question: Which traffic signal indicates you should slow down and proceed with caution at an intersection?
options: a:A flashing yellow light.,b:A flashing red light.,c:A solid yellow light.
note: A flashing yellow signal means slow down and proceed with caution; it does not require a full stop like a flashing red signal does.

question: How does eating or drinking while driving affect driving performance?
options: a:Improves concentration.,b:Has no effect.,c:Increases the chance of lane and control errors.,d:Makes it easier to maintain speed.
note: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving distracts your hands and eyes from driving tasks, increasing the likelihood of lane drift and loss of vehicle control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the usual speed limit in school zones unless otherwise posted?
options: a:25 mph.,b:35 mph.,c:45 mph.
note: Unless a different speed is posted, the speed limit in school zones is 25 miles per hour; always exercise extra caution.

question: What color are highway guide signs that show distance to the next exit?
options: a:Green with white letters.,b:Yellow with black letters.,c:Black with white letters.,d:Red with white letters.
note: Guide and destination signs are green with white letters or symbols; they show directions and distances to destinations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about railroad crossings is correct?
options: a:It is lawful to go around lowered gates.,b:You must never stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger.,c:All of the following — you must stop when directed, not all crossings have signals, and it is illegal to go around lowered gates.
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger or when warning devices are activated. Not all crossings have gates or lights, and it is illegal to drive around lowered gates.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop where two drivers arrive simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.,b:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,c:Either driver may proceed without yielding.
note: Yield the right-of-way to the driver on your right when you arrive at the same time at a four-way stop.

question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first?
options: a:Turn your wheels toward the curb immediately.,b:Back in from far away without aligning.,c:Signal and stop in the middle of the street.,d:Pull up even with the car in front of the space and then begin turning into the spot.
note: After signaling and checking traffic, stop even with the vehicle ahead of the space, then back slowly while steering into the spot.

question: At an intersection, a flashing red light requires you to:
options: a:Slow down but keep moving.,b:Come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.,c:Wait for the light to turn green.
note: A flashing red signal is treated like a stop sign—stop fully, yield, and proceed only when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before making a turn you should:
options: a:Use your turn signal a few seconds before the turn.,b:Turn the wheel immediately without signaling.,c:Increase your speed before turning.
note: Signal three to four seconds (or about 100 feet) before turning to alert other road users of your intentions.

question: It is illegal for a person age 21 or older to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of at least:
options: a:0.05 percent.,b:0.08 percent.,c:0.02 percent.
note: For drivers 21 and older the legal limit in New Jersey is a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which lane-dividing line allows you to pass another vehicle traveling in the same direction?
options: a:Broken white line.,b:Solid yellow line.,c:Double solid yellow line.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to pass when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic light changes from green to solid yellow as you approach, how should you respond?
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection unless you are too close to stop safely.,b:Speed up to get through the intersection.,c:Consider it only a caution sign and continue at the same speed.
note: A steady yellow warns you that the signal will change to red; stop if you can do so safely, otherwise proceed with caution.

question: What color are guide or destination signs?
options: a:Yellow with black letters.,b:Blue with white letters.,c:Green with white letters.,d:Red with white letters.
note: Guide signs (destination signs) are green with white lettering and show directions and distances.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Driving well below the speed limit on a highway is:
options: a:Illegal if it impedes normal traffic flow.,b:Always the safest practice.,c:Recommended to avoid collisions.,d:Allowed even if it stops traffic.
note: Driving so slowly that you block the normal flow of traffic is against the law and creates a hazard.

question: Why must you use extra caution around a pedestrian carrying a white cane?
options: a:They are likely to be deaf.,b:They might be a police officer.,c:They are typically blind or visually impaired.
note: A pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog is usually blind or visually impaired. Slow down, yield the right-of-way, and be prepared to stop to avoid harm.

question: Why should you avoid following other cars too closely?
options: a:You may not see the road between the cars.,b:You may not have enough time to stop if the vehicle in front slows or stops suddenly.,c:You may not see the vehicle's turn signals.
note: Tailgating reduces your reaction time and stopping distance; maintain a safe following distance to avoid rear-end collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit in suburban business districts is typically closest to:
options: a:70 mph.,b:55 mph.,c:40 mph.
note: Common suburban business district limits are usually lower (around 35 mph); if a different limit is posted, follow the sign.

question: If the driver ahead is distracted (one hand on wheel, talking to a passenger), what should you do?
options: a:Give the vehicle extra space.,b:Know they have increased their safety margin.,c:Copy the driver's behavior.
note: If a nearby driver appears distracted, allow extra space because their risk of causing an accident is higher.

question: Between what hours may a person with a valid learner permit drive?
options: a:Between 12:01 a.m. and 5:00 a.m.,b:Between 9:00 a.m. and 9:00 p.m.,c:Between 5:00 a.m. and 11:00 p.m.
note: Learner permit holders may not drive between 11:00 p.m. and 5:00 a.m.; allowed hours are typically 5:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m. unless supervised practice rules differ.

question: If you are being tailgated, what is the best initial response if an open right lane exists?
options: a:Move over to the right lane if it is open.,b:Slow down abruptly to warn the tailgater.,c:Speed up to increase distance from the tailgater.
note: If a tailgater is behind you and a right lane is available, move over. If no lane is available, slow gradually to encourage them to pass; never brake suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against the signal, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.,b:Speed up to clear the intersection before pedestrians arrive.,c:Honk to make them hurry.
note: Yield to pedestrians even if they are crossing against the signal; avoid driving through pedestrians in an intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What general rule should you follow regarding passing other vehicles?
options: a:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when necessary and safe.,b:Always pass on the right whenever possible.,c:Try to get to the front of slow traffic to improve visibility.
note: Passing increases collision risk; drive with traffic flow within legal limits and pass only when needed and safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, you should:
options: a:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,b:Keep the front wheels straight and set the parking brake.,c:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb so a roll would cause the car to move away from traffic.

question: When driving through an area where children may be playing, what should you expect of their behavior?
options: a:They may run out in front of you without looking.,b:They will stop at the curb before crossing.,c:They will know when it is safe to cross the street.
note: Children may not understand or recognize danger; reduce speed and be prepared for them to dart into the street.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How long before changing lanes or passing should you signal?
options: a:At any random time.,b:Signal early enough to let others know your intentions.,c:Only after you start changing lanes.
note: Signal in advance of your maneuver so other drivers have adequate notice of your intentions.

question: A work zone:
options: a:May be moving or stationary and requires extra caution.,b:Is marked with black and white signs.,c:Does not require drivers to slow down.
note: Work zones can be stationary or moving, are typically marked with orange signs, and require drivers to slow down and pay close attention.

question: If a collision seems unavoidable, what is the preferred strategy?
options: a:Aim for something that will give way or try to make a glancing blow.,b:Brake hard and hope for the best.,c:Hit something that is stationary rather than moving.
note: If you cannot avoid a crash, try to strike something that will absorb impact (like shrubs) and aim for a glancing blow rather than a head-on collision.

question: A solid white edge line that slants inward toward the center of the road indicates what?
options: a:The roadway narrows ahead.,b:An upcoming intersection.,c:A construction area.
note: If the right-edge line angles toward the center, the road narrows ahead and you should be prepared to adjust.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive faster than what?
options: a:The maximum posted speed only.,b:Any speed if traffic is light.,c:Twice the speed limit during the day.,d:A speed that is reasonable and prudent given conditions.
note: You must drive at a speed that is reasonable and prudent for current conditions, not simply at the posted maximum if it is unsafe.

question: A flashing yellow arrow for left turns means:
options: a:You must come to a complete stop.,b:You may turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,c:You should merge immediately into the lane of the arrow.
note: A flashing yellow arrow permits left turns but requires you to yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.

question: To prevent your physical condition from causing unsafe driving, you should:
options: a:Know the effects of any medicines on your driving ability.,b:Ignore minor health issues while driving.,c:Avoid regular medical check-ups.
note: Be aware of how medications and health conditions affect your driving and drive within your physical limitations.

question: Which statement about emergency vehicles is correct?
options: a:You must yield the right-of-way when they use sirens or flashing lights.,b:You may always follow an emergency vehicle closely to get ahead.,c:You can ignore loudspeaker instructions from them.
note: Yield immediately to police cars, fire engines, and ambulances using sirens or flashing lights. Obey any instructions given by their loudspeakers.

question: Which of the following may be used on some highways to direct drivers into the correct lanes for turning?
options: a:White pavement edge lines.,b:Flashing yellow lights.,c:Flashing red lights.
note: Highways often use lane-arrow markings or special signal indications (such as arrow or flashing lane signals) to show which lanes are for turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, which vehicle has the right-of-way?
options: a:The car approaching from the right.,b:The car approaching from the left.,c:The car whose driver sounds the horn first.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, yield to traffic approaching from your right; that driver has the right-of-way.

question: When driving in bad weather, what change should you make to your following distance?
options: a:Keep the same following distance.,b:Increase the following distance.,c:Decrease the following distance.
note: Increase following distance in rain, snow, or fog to allow more time to react and stop safely.

question: Using which device greatly increases crash risk due to distraction?
options: a:Radio only.,b:Cell phone (including hands-free).,c:Turn signals.,d:CD player only.
note: Cell phone use (even hands-free) is a significant distraction and increases crash risk; any distracting device can be dangerous.

question: What can happen when alcohol is combined with another drug?
options: a:The effects of both substances will be reduced.,b:The effects of both substances may become stronger.,c:Nothing will happen.
note: Mixing alcohol with another drug can multiply the effects of both substances, increasing impairment and risk more than either alone.

question: Which types of drugs can impair your driving ability?
options: a:Only allergy medicine.,b:Only marijuana.,c:Illegal drugs and prescription or over-the-counter medications alike (all of the above).
note: Many substances — illegal drugs, prescription medicines, and over-the-counter remedies — can affect reaction time and driving ability.

question: On average, how much alcohol does the body eliminate per hour?
options: a:Three drinks per hour.,b:One standard drink per hour.,c:Two drinks per hour.,d:No alcohol is eliminated without sleep.
note: The average person metabolizes about one standard alcoholic drink per hour, though many factors (weight, food, health) influence impairment.

question: What must a driver produce when stopped for a violation or equipment check?
options: a:Only proof of registration.,b:Only proof of insurance.,c:License, proof of registration, and proof of insurance.
note: When stopped, the driver must provide their license, vehicle registration, and proof of insurance — all three documents should be available.

question: If your slow driving is causing a line of traffic to build up behind you on a two-lane, two-way road, what should you do?
options: a:Decrease your speed further.,b:Pull off to the right and allow traffic to pass.,c:Refuse to let other cars pass.
note: If you are impeding traffic by driving slower than the flow, you should safely pull off the road and let others pass. Only drive slow when conditions require it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an officer is directing traffic at a location where signals are working, what should drivers do?
options: a:Follow the officer's directions instead of the traffic lights.,b:Follow only the traffic light indications.,c:Honk to get the officer's attention.
note: When an officer is directing traffic, obey the officer's signals even if they conflict with the traffic lights.

question: Lines that divide lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions are what color?
options: a:Red.,b:Black.,c:White.,d:Yellow.
note: Yellow pavement markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions; white lines separate traffic going the same direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do if you miss your exit or turn on a freeway?
options: a:Make a rapid turn from your lane of travel.,b:Stop and back up on the shoulder.,c:Continue to the next exit or other safe location to turn around.
note: If you miss an exit, do not back up or stop on the freeway; continue to the next exit where it is safe to leave and turn around.

question: What are the typical colors of warning signs that notify you of upcoming hazards?
options: a:Black on white.,b:Black symbols or letters on a yellow background.,c:White on blue.
note: General warning signs are yellow with black symbols or letters; work zone warnings are orange with black symbols.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you're waiting in the intersection to make a left turn, how should you position your wheels?
options: a:Signal and keep your wheels turned to the left.,b:Signal and keep your wheels straight.,c:Flash your headlights to ask drivers to let you through.
note: Keep your wheels straight while waiting to make a left turn. If hit from behind, straight wheels reduce the chance of being pushed into oncoming traffic.

question: What does a solid yellow line next to your lane mean?
options: a:You may pass with caution.,b:Passing is prohibited from your direction.,c:This lane is for buses only.,d:You must slow down.
note: A solid yellow line on your side of center indicates you may not pass from that lane.

question: What does a double solid yellow line down the center of a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Opposite directions and no passing is permitted.,b:Opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.,c:Same direction traffic and no passing allowed.
note: Yellow center lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Double solid lines indicate passing is prohibited for both directions.

question: What do downward-facing triangular traffic signs indicate?
options: a:School zones.,b:Yield to other traffic.,c:Construction zones.
note: A downward-pointing triangle is used for yield signs, indicating you must yield to other vehicles or pedestrians when appropriate.

question: What color pavement markings separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:White.,b:Yellow and white together.,c:Yellow.
note: Yellow pavement markings are used to separate traffic moving in opposite directions; white lines separate same-direction lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an oncoming vehicle is driving toward you in your lane, what should you do first?
options: a:Flash your lights and keep going.,b:You honking,c:Brake firmly and stay in your lane.,d:Honking
note: If a vehicle is coming at you head-on, honk to warn the driver, try to move right to avoid a collision, and brake firmly. Every mph you reduce lowers the impact.

question: How can you avoid collisions caused by vehicles in your blind spots?
options: a:Quickly turn your head to check the blind spot before changing lanes.,b:Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.,c:Sound your horn before changing lanes.
note: Before turning or changing lanes, glance over your shoulder toward the lane you intend to enter to check the blind spot; do not rely on mirrors alone.

question: What must you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights approaches?
options: a:See if you can reach your destination before it catches you.,b:Continue driving and try to stay out of its way.,c:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
note: Yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights by pulling over to the right and stopping; if in an intersection, clear it first and then pull over.

question: When involved in a collision, you should:
options: a:Move injured people to a more comfortable position.,b:Avoid moving the injured unless absolutely necessary.,c:Only call emergency services if the vehicles are badly damaged.
note: Unless there is an immediate danger (e.g., fire), do not move injured persons; call emergency services right away.

question: What should you adjust first when you get into a car to drive?
options: a:Your seat.,b:The steering wheel.,c:Your rearview mirror.
note: Adjust your seat first so you can reach the controls comfortably and see the road clearly; then adjust mirrors and the steering wheel if needed.

question: How do worn or bald tires affect driving?
options: a:They improve fuel economy.,b:They reduce risk of skidding.,c:They only affect top speed.,d:They increase stopping distance, make turning harder, and heighten hydroplaning risk.
note: Tires lacking tread increase stopping distances, reduce traction for turning, and are more likely to hydroplane on wet roads.

question: If your vehicle's accelerator sticks while driving, what is the correct immediate action?
options: a:Blow your horn to warn others.,b:Turn off the ignition while steering to a safe area and apply brakes carefully.,c:Slam on your brakes immediately.
note: If the accelerator sticks, steer to a safe area, turn off the ignition (being careful not to lock the steering), slow and stop, then apply the parking brake once controlled.

question: How long must a driver age 21 or older practicing under a GDL complete supervised driving before taking the road test?
options: a:One month.,b:Six months.,c:Three months.
note: Drivers age 21 or older under the GDL must complete a minimum of three months of supervised driving before the road test.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles enter an intersection from different highways at the same time, who must yield?
options: a:The driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.,b:Either driver as they choose.,c:The driver on the right yields to the left.,d:The larger vehicle yields.
note: If two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

question: On a vertically arranged traffic light, what is the correct top-to-bottom order of colors?
options: a:Red,b:Green,c:You red
note: Vertically arranged signals have red on top, yellow in the middle, and green on the bottom.

question: When is it permitted to drive around lowered gates at a railroad crossing?
options: a:Only after the train has passed and gates are fully raised.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:Once the lights stop flashing, even if gates remain down.
note: You must never go around a lowered crossing gate. Stop and wait until the gates are raised and the lights have stopped flashing.

question: When pedestrians are in a crosswalk marked by two solid white lines, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Motor vehicles have the right-of-way.,b:No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.,c:Pedestrians should be given the right-of-way.
note: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians who are in a marked crosswalk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a green arrow changes to a solid green light, what must you do to turn?
options: a:You may still turn but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:You may no longer turn and must go straight.,c:You retain the right-of-way to turn without yielding.
note: A solid green allows turns in the arrow's direction but you must yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From the center lane marked for turns, which maneuvers are permitted?
options: a:Using it to pass slow-moving traffic.,b:Using it for through-traffic.,c:Making left turns from either direction when the center lane is designated for left turns.
note: A center two-way left-turn lane is for completing left turns into or out of the roadway, not for passing or through traffic.

question: How can stress affect your driving?
options: a:By lowering your ability to focus on driving tasks.,b:By decreasing your chance of having an accident.,c:By causing you to fall asleep at the wheel.
note: Stress and strong emotions can reduce concentration and impair driving ability; wait until you are calmer before driving.

question: If you are driving in the left lane and want to move into the right lane, you should:
options: a:Check mirrors,b:Look in mirrors,c:Check rear view
note: When moving to the right, check mirrors, signal, and glance over your right shoulder to check the blind spot before changing lanes.

question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means what?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken line.,b:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid line.,c:Passing is allowed from either lane at any time.
note: If the broken line is beside your lane, you may pass when it is safe; the solid line prohibits passing from that side.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a steady yellow traffic light, what is the correct action?
options: a:Speed up to clear the intersection.,b:Ignore it and continue at the same speed.,c:Back up to avoid the red light.,d:Slow to a stop unless you are already in the intersection.
note: A steady yellow warns that the signal will change to red; stop if you can safely do so, unless you are already in the intersection.

question: If you must stop along the road at night, you should:
options: a:Turn off all lights.,b:Use only your parking lights.,c:Leave your low-beam headlights on and activate emergency flashers.
note: When stopped at night make your vehicle visible by leaving low beams on and turning on hazard flashers so approaching drivers can see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle with the blinker on.,b:The faster vehicle.,c:The larger vehicle.,d:The vehicle on the right has the right-of-way; the vehicle on the left yields.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

question: How does increasing your vehicle’s speed affect your field of vision?
options: a:It decreases your field of vision and narrows peripheral awareness.,b:It increases your field of vision.,c:It makes it easier to see cross traffic.,d:It has no effect on vision.
note: As speed increases, your field of vision narrows, requiring greater alertness to potential hazards.

question: When negotiating turns on slick or slippery roads, you should:
options: a:Take turns more slowly than usual.,b:Accelerate quickly through the turn.,c:Change lanes quickly before the turn.
note: On slippery roads reduce speed before entering curves and turns and make smooth, cautious steering and braking inputs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the light is green but oncoming traffic is heavy when you want to turn left, what should you do?
options: a:Use the next intersection instead of turning.,b:Enter the intersection on green and wait to complete the left turn when it is safe.,c:Wait in the crosswalk for traffic to clear.
note: You may enter the intersection on a green light to prepare for a left turn if it is safe and there is no vehicle ahead intending to turn; then yield to oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes or turning, what must you always do?
options: a:Signal your intentions every time, even if you see no traffic.,b:Signal only when other vehicles are present.,c:Signal only at night.
note: You must always signal before changing lanes, turning, or pulling away from a curb. Signaling every time prevents bad habits and increases safety.

question: What is the most common color used for warning signs?
options: a:Red.,b:Yellow.,c:Green.
note: Warning signs are most often diamond-shaped and yellow with black markings to alert drivers to unexpected conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road should do what?
options: a:Yield to drivers already on the public road and merge when safe.,b:Assume the right-of-way and force entry, c:Always stop with part of their car on the roadway to warn others.
note: Yield to vehicles on the public road when entering from a private driveway; merge only when it is safe.

question: How can drowsiness affect a driver's ability to operate a vehicle?
options: a:Opening a window or turning up the radio will keep you alert.,b:Drowsy drivers can operate so poorly they resemble drunk drivers.,c:Drinking coffee is a reliable way to remain awake while driving.
note: Drowsiness impairs driving and can make a driver appear intoxicated. Measures like opening a window, turning up the radio, or drinking coffee are not reliable ways to stay alert.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Oncoming traffic.,b:Only to vehicles already stopped in the intersection.,c:Only to pedestrians who are already in the intersection.
note: When turning left you must yield to oncoming vehicles as well as to any pedestrians in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Always use your turn signal when which of the following maneuvers?
options: a:Changing lanes.,b:Only when turning left.,c:Only when parking on a public street.
note: Always signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of parking spaces, or entering traffic from an alley or driveway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering the interstate from an entrance ramp should:
options: a:Yield to drivers already on the interstate.,b:Force their way into traffic because they are on the ramp.,c:Assume they have the right-of-way.
note: When merging from an entrance or acceleration lane, yield to traffic already on the highway and merge safely when there is a gap.

question: If your windshield wipers fail during rain or snow, what should you do first?
options: a:Slow down, pull off the roadway to a safe area, and use your emergency flashers.,b:Brake and stop immediately in the travel lane.,c:Roll down the driver's window and put your head out to see ahead.
note: Slow down, pull over to a safe place off the road, turn on emergency flashers, and call for assistance if necessary.

question: What effect does alcohol have on driving ability?
options: a:It slows reflexes and reaction time.,b:It wakes you up and increases alertness.,c:It improves night vision.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain activity, impairs judgment, and reduces reaction time needed for safe driving.

question: What is one way to help prevent crashes involving other road users?
options: a:Communicate with other road users by signaling and using your horn when appropriate.,b:Ignore other drivers on the road.,c:Drive only on side streets and back roads.
note: Use signals, brake lights, horn, and eye contact when safe to communicate your intentions and avoid unexpected actions that lead to crashes.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing while in a line of traffic with no gates or signals, what must you ensure?
options: a:You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.,b:There is enough space for your vehicle to clear all tracks without stopping.,c:You may pass slower vehicles while crossing the tracks.
note: Make sure there is room to fully cross the tracks before you enter; never stop on the tracks and never pass another vehicle while crossing.

question: If sleet or snow begins while you are driving, you should:
options: a:Approach other vehicles with caution.,b:Keep windshield and mirrors clear and allow extra following distance.,c:Maintain normal following distance because conditions are unchanged.
note: In wintry conditions keep windows and mirrors clear, reduce speed, and increase following distance to allow longer stopping distances.

question: What happens to tire effectiveness on a wet roadway as you increase speed?
options: a:Tires become less effective at clearing water and may cause hydroplaning.,b:Water has no effect on cars with good tires.,c:Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
note: As speed increases on wet roads, tires struggle to clear water, increasing the risk of hydroplaning.

question: What should be your first response to reduced visibility?
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Turn on your windshield wipers.,c:Turn on headlights.
note: Your first action should be to slow down when visibility decreases; then use lights and wipers as needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before passing another vehicle on a multilane highway, what should you verify?
options: a:You should always increase speed drastically to pass.,b:You may only pass on the right on multilane highways.,c:There is oncoming traffic in the opposite lane.,d:The passing lane is clear and it is safe to move over.
note: Ensure the lane you plan to move into is clear, signal, and complete the pass safely.

question: If your vehicle's turn signals stop working, what should you use to show other drivers your intended turn?
options: a:Hand signals.,b:Your horn.,c:Your headlights.
note: If the electronic turn signals are inoperative, use standard hand signals to indicate left or right turns and stops.

question: Why is maintaining a space cushion around your vehicle important?
options: a:It prevents distractions from other vehicles.,b:It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.,c:It keeps traffic flowing at a set pace.
note: A space cushion allows time and room to react to mistakes or sudden moves by other road users, reducing the chance of collisions.

question: A pedestrian begins crossing in front of your car. What should you do?
options: a:Flash your lights to warn them.,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,c:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
note: Always slow and be prepared to stop for pedestrians, especially in crosswalks; yield the right-of-way to pedestrians crossing legally.

question: How does alcohol affect driving skills and judgment?
options: a:It helps driving skills but harms judgment.,b:It harms both driving skills and judgment.,c:It has no effect on either skill or judgment.
note: Alcohol impairs coordination, reaction time, vision, concentration, and judgement, making driving unsafe.

question: When driving near heavy trucks, what must other drivers allow for?
options: a:The truck’s increased stopping distance and larger blind spots.,b:That trucks can stop more quickly than cars.,c:That they produce less noise than cars.,d:That trucks will always maintain posted speeds.
note: Give large trucks extra space for their longer stopping distances and be mindful of their blind spots so the truck driver can see you.

question: When passing a vehicle that has just parked at the curb, what should you assume?
options: a:The parked driver may open a car door as you approach, so use extra caution.,b:The driver will wait until you pass, so you can speed up.,c:You should slam on your brakes to avoid doors opening.
note: Assume occupants may open doors; slow slightly and give extra clearance when passing parked vehicles.

question: What does a flashing red traffic signal require you to do?
options: a:Stop completely and proceed only when it is safe (same as a stop sign).,b:Assume the traffic signal is broken and proceed without stopping.,c:Slow down but you do not have to stop.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign: stop completely, yield as necessary, and go only when safe.

question: When must you turn your headlights on?
options: a:Only when you cannot see other vehicles.,b:Only when driving in heavy traffic.,c:From one-half hour after sunset until one-half hour before sunrise, and any time visibility is 500 feet or less or wipers are on.
note: Use headlights from 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise, or when visibility drops below 500 feet, and whenever wipers are in use.

question: What should drivers remember about large trucks?
options: a:They have extensive blind spots and need more room to maneuver and stop.,b:They can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.,c:They require no additional room to maneuver compared to smaller cars.
note: Large trucks have big blind spots to the front, sides, and rear and require more distance to stop and maneuver than passenger vehicles.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, you should:
options: a:Overcorrect to compensate.,b:Turn the steering wheel into oncoming traffic.,c:Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the skid.
note: If your vehicle skids, steer gently in the direction of the skid until you regain traction, then correct back to center.

question: Before backing out of your driveway with children nearby, what should you do before moving the car?
options: a:Walk to the back of the car and verify the way is clear.,b:Rev your engine to warn children that you are moving.,c:Sound your horn so the children will hear you.
note: When backing up, always look through the rear window and, especially with children nearby, get out and check behind the vehicle instead of relying only on mirrors.

question: What should you do when approaching an accident scene?
options: a:Keep moving without regard to the scene.,b:Stop only if you are involved or if emergency help has not yet arrived.,c:Keep your attention on driving and move past the scene.
note: Do not stop at an accident unless you are involved or are needed and emergency help has not arrived. Keep moving while watching for people near the road.

question: Under the GDL (Graduated Driver License) rules, what is a driver with a GDL prohibited from doing?
options: a:Driving only during daytime.,b:Not wearing a seat belt at all times.,c:Using any hand-held or hands-free cell phone while driving.
note: Drivers with a GDL may not use electronic devices while driving; all drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.

question: Which of the following is least helpful in promoting safe night driving?
options: a:Keeping your windshield clean.,b:Being aware that tinted windows reduce night visibility.,c:Relying on a flashlight instead of vehicle lights while driving.
note: Keep windows clean, reduce glare, and ensure proper vehicle lighting; carrying a flashlight is useful but does not replace proper vehicle lights for safe night driving.

question: When borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Hide from the owner that you are unfamiliar with the vehicle.,b:Ignore any unusual controls and drive normally.,c:Familiarize yourself with the vehicle's controls and check for defects.
note: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, take time to find and test lights, signals, wipers, brakes, gear selector, and horn; fix any defects before use.

question: When driving in fog, you should:
options: a:Use your high beams.,b:Drive cautiously and reduce your speed using low beams.,c:Turn on your hazard lights.
note: Fog reduces visibility significantly; use low beams (not high beams) and slow down to maintain safe control and sight distance.

question: If your car breaks down on a highway, you should:
options: a:Sit inside and wait for help.,b:Use your four-way flashers to warn other drivers and move safely off the road.,c:Sound your horn to attract attention.
note: Signal, move your vehicle well off the traveled portion of the road, turn on emergency flashers, and use other warning means to alert other drivers.

question: On long trips, how can you reduce drowsiness while driving?
options: a:Turn up the radio volume continuously.,b:Rely on caffeine only.,c:Slow down significantly.,d:Stop regularly to rest and stretch.
note: Schedule regular stops to rest, walk, and stretch to prevent drowsiness on long trips.

question: When preparing to change lanes, which of the following is important to do?
options: a:Signal your intentions well before the lane change.,b:Change lanes and then signal.,c:Rely only on your mirrors.
note: Signal in advance, check mirrors and blind spots, and make sure the lane is clear before you move.

question: How should drivers react to a steady yellow arrow?
options: a:Merge into the lane indicated by the arrow.,b:Slow to a stop, if it is safe to do so.,c:Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: A steady yellow arrow warns that a red arrow is about to appear. Stop if you can do so safely; otherwise clear the intersection.

question: Which of the following is NOT an effect of drinking alcohol?
options: a:Improved alertness.,b:Slower reflexes and reaction time.,c:Distorted judgement of speed and distance.
note: Alcohol impairs vision, slows reaction time, and distorts judgement. It does not improve alertness.

question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights of an approaching emergency vehicle, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down until it passes.,b:Drive to the right side of the road and stop.,c:Motion for the vehicle to pass you.
note: You must immediately drive to the right side of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed; if in an intersection, clear it before pulling over.

question: You do not need to stop for a frozen dessert truck when:
options: a:You are on the opposite side of a divided highway separated by a raised median or safety island.,b:It shows flashing red lights and has its stop arm extended.,c:A person is crossing the roadway to or from the truck.
note: If the truck is on the opposite side of a divided highway separated by a median, you are not required to stop; otherwise, when it displays red lights or a stop arm or someone is crossing, you must stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road or driveway?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic before entering.,b:Stop with part of your vehicle on the roadway to alert drivers.,c:Drive quickly into traffic to merge smoothly.
note: When entering from a driveway or private road, always yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and vehicles already on the roadway and merge only when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, which driver has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver who arrived first.,b:The driver who arrived last.,c:The driver on the left if two arrived together.
note: At four-way stops the first vehicle to arrive goes first. If two arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the right has right-of-way.

question: When should you reduce speed for a curve in the road?
options: a:Before entering the curve.,b:After exiting the curve.,c:Only if another car is beside you.,d:When you are halfway through the curve.
note: Adjust your speed before entering a curve; entering too fast can cause loss of traction and control.

question: How long must a driver practice unsupervised driving on a probationary license before obtaining a basic driver license?
options: a:Nine months.,b:One year.,c:Five months.
note: A probationary license holder must practice unsupervised driving for at least one year before eligibility for a basic driver license.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a multi-lane roadway with merging traffic, what is the appropriate action?
options: a:Always remain at your present speed.,b:Hon k at incoming traffic.,c:Move over or adjust speed to make room for entering vehicles.
note: When possible, make room for vehicles entering the roadway from ramps; change lanes if safe or adjust speed to allow them to merge.

question: What best ensures safety when backing a vehicle?
options: a:Walk behind the vehicle to check for children or objects before getting in, then use mirrors when backing.,b:Honk just before shifting to reverse.,c:Only check rearview mirrors after you begin backing.,d:Back quickly to finish sooner.
note: Before getting in to back up, walk around and check behind the vehicle for children or objects; then use mirrors and proceed slowly.

question: Why should drivers be extra alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?
options: a:They are smaller and more difficult to see in traffic.,b:They obey different traffic laws.,c:They always have the right-of-way.,d:They travel only at night.
note: Smaller road users are harder to spot and may be hidden in blind spots; be especially cautious around them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you approach a railroad crossing?
options: a:Slow down.,b:Look for a train.,c:Be prepared to stop (all of the above).
note: Upon seeing signs for a railroad crossing, slow down, look and listen for trains, and be ready to stop. If gates/lights are activated, stop 15–50 feet from the tracks.

question: When passing a bicyclist on the roadway, what is the safest practice?
options: a:Slow down and give the bicyclist as much space as possible when passing.,b:Drive in the bicycle lane until you pass.,c:Honk at the bicyclist to signal your presence.
note: Bicyclists are vulnerable road users; slow down and provide plenty of lateral clearance when passing.

question: Many crashes are caused by what driving behavior?
options: a:Traveling too fast for current conditions.,b:Constantly checking mirrors and blind spots.,c:Yielding the right-of-way.
note: Driving too fast for conditions is a common factor in crashes. Adjust speed to match road and weather conditions.

question: What does a diamond-shaped traffic sign normally indicate?
options: a:A road hazard or warning sign.,b:An interstate route sign.,c:A school crossing sign.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are typically warning signs (yellow or orange) that alert drivers to potential hazards or changes in the roadway.

question: A solid red arrow displayed by a traffic signal means:
options: a:Drivers may turn in the arrow's direction.,b:It has the same meaning as a circular red light.,c:It is never used in traffic signals.
note: A solid red arrow means traffic in that lane must stop and may not proceed in the direction indicated by the arrow.

question: What combination of safety restraints is most effective in a crash?
options: a:Only a lap and shoulder belt.,b:Only an airbag.,c:Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
note: Seat belts significantly increase survival rates in crashes; airbags provide additional protection when used with lap and shoulder belts.

question: A driver who travels much slower than the flow of traffic:
options: a:Is a very safe driver.,b:Always has the right-of-way.,c:Should allow following vehicles to pass when appropriate.
note: Driving much slower than surrounding traffic can be hazardous; you should pull over when safe to let traffic pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
