question: If traffic signals are out due to a power outage, how should you treat the intersection?
options: a:Park and wait for power to return.,b:Turn on your hazard lights and proceed without stopping.,c:As you would a four-way stop—yield and proceed in order.
note: When signals fail, treat the intersection like a four-way stop: stop, yield, and proceed when it's your turn and safe.

question: Why must you be especially alert for motorcycles?
options: a:They are smaller and harder to see and their speed/distance is harder to judge.,b:They rarely obey traffic signals.,c:Motorcyclists always have less experience.,d:They can stop instantly unlike cars.
note: Motorcycles are smaller and can be hidden in blind spots; it can be difficult to judge their speed and distance, so take extra caution.

question: If another car is about to hit you, what is the primary action to warn them?
options: a:Sound your horn.,b:Wave your arms.,c:Turn on your emergency lights.
note: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians of an immediate danger when an accident appears imminent.

question: If your vehicle is blocking traffic after an accident, you should:
options: a:Move the vehicle off the traveled portion of the roadway, if possible.,b:Never move the vehicle under any circumstances.,c:Wait for police to move it.
note: After a minor collision and if it is safe, move vehicles out of the travel lanes to prevent further incidents; still exchange information and report as required.

question: Under poor weather conditions, how much longer may it take a tractor-trailer to stop compared to ideal conditions?
options: a:10% longer.,b:25% longer.,c:40% longer.,d:5% longer.
note: In poor weather, a tractor-trailer may require up to about 25% more stopping distance than under ideal conditions, so give them extra space.

question: The effect of severe sleep deprivation on driving is comparable to:
options: a:The effect that alcohol has.,b:The effect of taking amphetamines.,c:The effect of being angry.
note: Lack of sleep impairs judgment and reaction time similar to alcohol intoxication; prolonged wakefulness can be as impairing as a measurable BAC.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving on an interstate, what should you do before changing lanes?
options: a:Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.,b:Always use cruise control.,c:Signal, check mirrors, and check your blind spot.
note: Before changing lanes on a highway, always signal, check mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to verify blind spots are clear.

question: Which action can help avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?
options: a:Engage your vehicle's four-wheel drive if equipped.,b:Add extra weight to improve traction.,c:Get off the highways as quickly as possible.
note: Reducing speed and increasing following distance are most important; using four-wheel drive can help where appropriate but does not replace safe driving techniques.

question: If your vehicle starts to skid, you should turn the steering wheel:
options: a:In the direction you want the vehicle to go.,b:To keep the front wheels straight.,c:In the opposite direction of the skid.
note: Steer in the direction you want the vehicle to move to regain traction, then correct gradually to center.

question: Which factors influence the effects of alcohol on a person?
options: a:Amount of food in the stomach, body weight, and time between drinks.,b:The brand of alcohol consumed.,c:Whether you are in a moving vehicle.
note: BAC and intoxication level depend on how much you drink, your body weight, time between drinks, and whether you ate, among other factors.

question: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim its high beams, what is the safest action?
options: a:Glance toward the right side of the road until the vehicle passes.,b:Look toward the center of the road directly at the lights.,c:Flash your high beams to warn the other driver.
note: Look away from the bright lights toward the right edge of the roadway to avoid being blinded and maintain your lane position.

question: What is the practice of turning your head to check a blind spot before changing lanes called?
options: a:An unnecessary action.,b:A bad driving habit.,c:A good driving habit.
note: Checking blind spots by turning your head over your shoulder before changing lanes, merging, or leaving a curb complements mirror checks and increases safety.

question: How should drivers treat a flashing red traffic light?
options: a:Treat it as a yield signal.,b:Like a stop sign: come to a complete stop, then proceed when safe.,c:Continue through if there is no crossing traffic.
note: A flashing red signal requires a full stop, yielding to other traffic and pedestrians, and then proceeding when the way is clear.

question: If your brakes fail while driving, what is the first action you should try?
options: a:Shift to a higher gear and press the gas.,b:Turn off the engine immediately.,c:Switch to neutral and coast.,d:Shift to a lower gear and pump the brake pedal.
note: If brakes fail, shift to a lower gear and try repeatedly pumping the brake pedal to build pressure; find a safe place to stop.

question: If you drive while your license is suspended and cause injury to another person, what are potential consequences?
options: a:You will receive only a warning.,b:You will only have to pay a fine.,c:You may be fined, receive an extended suspension, and be jailed.
note: Operating a vehicle with a suspended license is a serious offense; involvement in an injury crash can result in fines, extended suspension, and jail time.

question: At a stop sign, in which sequence should you look before proceeding?
options: a:Check your rearview mirror for tailgaters first.,b:Move when the vehicle ahead moves.,c:Look left first, then right, then left again.
note: When stopped at an intersection, check left first because vehicles from that side are usually closer, then right, then left again before proceeding.

question: How can you reduce the need to make an emergency stop in traffic?
options: a:Honk your horn to clear the lane ahead, c:Remain in the right lane at all times.,b:Look ahead and maintain a safe following distance.
note: A safe following distance gives you time to react to problems ahead without needing sudden emergency stops.

question: Your blind spot is the area:
options: a:You cannot see without moving your head.,b:Directly behind your vehicle only.,c:That is visible in your rearview mirror.
note: Blind spots are areas to the sides or rear that you cannot see using mirrors alone and require a quick shoulder check.

question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, what must you do with the ignition?
options: a:Lock the ignition and remove the key.,b:Turn off the engine only.,c:Set the parking brake only.
note: When leaving a vehicle unattended you must stop the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to pass another vehicle, you should:
options: a:Check your mirrors and blind spots before changing lanes.,b:Honk your horn repeatedly before passing.,c:Re-enter your lane within ten feet of the passed vehicle.
note: Before passing, check mirrors, signal, check blind spots, and only return to your lane when it is safe to do so and you can see the passed vehicle ahead in your rearview.

question: If there are two sets of railroad tracks side by side, what should you do after one train passes?
options: a:Assume it is safe to cross right away.,b:Look for another train on the other track before crossing.,c:Drive around lowered gates if clear.,d:Cross immediately to avoid another train.
note: After one train passes, check for a second train on the adjacent track before proceeding; do not cross until it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it acceptable to park or stop on the shoulder of a freeway?
options: a:Only if you turn on your four-way emergency flashers.,b:Only if no part of your vehicle is on the road.,c:Only in the case of an emergency.
note: Parking or stopping on a freeway shoulder is prohibited except in an emergency. If you must stop, use hazard flashers and get help as soon as possible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it permissible to avoid a traffic signal by driving on public or private property?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:If the property owner permits it.,c:Only if you are running late.
note: It is a traffic violation to drive on public or private property to avoid a traffic control signal or sign, except as directed by an officer.

question: Failing to yield to a pedestrian in a crosswalk can result in:
options: a:Only a warning.,b:Only points against your license.,c:Fines, points, possible jail time, community service, and license suspension.
note: Failing to yield to pedestrians can lead to fines, points on your license, community service, and possible jail and license suspension depending on severity.

question: If your vehicle's wheels drop off the pavement edge, how should you regain the road safely?
options: a:Continue with the wheels off the pavement, gently reduce speed, and when safe steer back onto the pavement.,b:Jerk the steering wheel and force the vehicle back onto the pavement immediately.,c:Slam on the brakes and stop.
note: Keep control, reduce speed gradually, then steer back onto the roadway when it is safe to do so—avoid sudden steering or braking.

question: How should drivers regard railroad crossings?
options: a:Safe to cross most of the time.,b:Dangerous; always be alert.,c:Good places to park temporarily.
note: Railroad crossings should always be treated with caution: look, listen, and be prepared to stop for approaching trains.

question: Smoking or preparing to smoke while driving:
options: a:Are distracting activities that can take your hands or eyes off the road.,b:Do not affect driving abilities.,c:Help drivers remain alert.
note: Smoking while driving can distract you by requiring you to take your hands off the wheel or your eyes off the road, increasing crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light, who must yield?
options: a:The driver must yield to the pedestrian.,b:The pedestrian must yield to the turning vehicle.,c:Whoever started moving last must yield.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing the roadway, even if there is no traffic signal, to avoid collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road with opposite traffic, when should you return to your lane?
options: a:Return to your lane when there is enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.,b:Remain in the left lane if you intend to turn left ahead.,c:Return immediately to the right side as soon as possible even if close to the other car.
note: After passing, move back into the driving lane only when you can safely re-enter with adequate space between you and the passed vehicle.

question: If a tire blows out while driving, what is the correct immediate action?
options: a:Slam on the brakes.,b:Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow to a stop gradually.,c:Keep driving at the same speed.
note: If a tire blows out, grip the wheel, stay in your lane, gradually reduce speed by easing off the accelerator and lightly braking once under control, then pull off the road.

question: What can happen to a bicyclist who disobeys traffic laws?
options: a:They are exempt from traffic laws.,b:They may be ticketed.,c:They will always receive only a warning.
note: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers. Those who disobey traffic laws can be cited by law enforcement.

question: When you hear or see an emergency vehicle approaching, what should you do?
options: a:Drive as far to the right as safely possible and stop.,b:Stop immediately wherever you are.,c:Continue slowly in your lane to let it pass.
note: On two-lane or undivided highways, pull far right and stop as soon as it is safe; do not stop in the middle of an intersection.

question: What does a single dashed yellow center line mean for drivers?
options: a:Both lanes travel in the same direction.,b:Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.,c:Drivers may not pass under any circumstances.
note: A single dashed yellow line separates opposite-direction traffic and indicates passing is permitted when it is safe and does not interfere with oncoming traffic.

question: What helps a person overcome the influence of alcoholic drinks?
options: a:Tomato juice.,b:Hot coffee.,c:Only the passage of time.,d:Fresh air and rest for 10 minutes.
note: Nothing sobers a person faster than time; coffee or fresh air do not reduce blood alcohol concentration.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you proceed through an intersection that has a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk?
options: a:After slowing down to verify there is no cross traffic.,b:After coming to a complete stop and confirming it is safe to proceed.,c:After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.
note: If a stop sign controls an intersection and no stop line or crosswalk exists, stop before entering the intersection and go only when it is safe.

question: Which behavior best describes a good defensive driver?
options: a:Driving slowly at all times.,b:Looking out for the actions of other drivers and anticipating problems.,c:Maintaining one constant speed regardless of conditions.,d:Tailgating slower vehicles to prevent lane changes.
note: Defensive drivers anticipate others' actions and remain alert to potential hazards, rather than simply driving slowly.

question: Which of the following helps prevent hydroplaning?
options: a:Reducing your speed in wet conditions.,b:Only checking tire tread once a year.,c:Keeping tires significantly underinflated.
note: To reduce hydroplaning risk, reduce speed in rain, ensure tires have good tread, and keep them properly inflated.

question: How should you react if you encounter an animal on the roadway?
options: a:No special action is required.,b:Sound your horn continuously.,c:Pass slowly and cautiously to avoid startling it.
note: Be very cautious around animals on the road; slow and pass at a safe distance to avoid startling the animal and causing an accident.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.,b:When exiting an expressway only.,c:Only when following a motorcycle.
note: Increase following distance behind large vehicles, in bad weather, heavy traffic, when exiting expressways, or when being tailgated.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing warning sign, how should you prepare?
options: a:Increase speed to clear the crossing quickly.,b:Look for ways to go around lowered gates.,c:Try to beat the train if gates are up.,d:Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.
note: Railroad warning signs alert you to the potential for a train; slow down and be ready to stop if necessary. Never go around barriers.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaching, what must you do?
options: a:Pull to the right curb and stop.,b:Slow down and remain driving in your lane.,c:Keep driving at the same speed.
note: You must immediately pull over to the curb or side of the road and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass.

question: When does your vehicle’s stopping distance increase?
options: a:On wet or icy roads and on loose gravel.,b:On paved dry highways at noon.,c:Only when driving downhill.,d:When following in empty parking lots.
note: Stopping distance is longer on wet, icy, or loose surfaces, and increases with speed and reduced traction.

question: You hear a siren from behind while driving—what action should you take?
options: a:Safely pull over to the right and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass.,b:Stop immediately in your lane.,c:Speed up to get out of the way.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches, create a clear path by pulling over to the right and stopping if safe to do so.

question: What does a steady yellow light at an intersection indicate?
options: a:The light is about to turn red; slow and prepare to stop.,b:Go through the intersection quickly.,c:Yield to traffic only when turning left.
note: A steady yellow warns that the light will change to red; slow down and prepare to stop unless you cannot do so safely.

question: An arrow painted on the pavement in a traffic lane indicates:
options: a:Drivers in that lane may choose to make the movement indicated by the arrow.,b:Drivers in that lane must make the movement indicated by the arrow.,c:Drivers must always stop before making the movement shown by the arrow.,d:The arrow applies only when traffic signals are not working.
note: A pavement arrow in a lane directs drivers in that lane to make the movement shown; always obey pavement markings along with any traffic signs or signals.

question: If an approaching driver fails to dim high beams, you should look:
options: a:At the approaching vehicle's wheels.,b:Toward the right side of the road.,c:Toward the left side of the road.
note: Glance toward the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded by the other vehicle's high beams while maintaining lane position.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where should slower-moving traffic drive on a multilane highway?
options: a:In the left lane.,b:In the right lane.,c:In whichever lane has less traffic.,d:In the center lane only.
note: On multilane roads, slower traffic should use the right lane so faster vehicles can pass on the left.

question: A probationary driver under 21 may transport which passengers?
options: a:Their dependents and one additional passenger.,b:Up to three additional passengers.,c:Up to four additional passengers.
note: Probationary drivers under 21 may carry their dependents and one additional passenger, per GDL restrictions.

question: What is the minimum age to register a vehicle in New Jersey?
options: a:18 years.,b:25 years.,c:17 years.
note: In New Jersey, you must be at least 17 to register a motor vehicle and provide proof of identity and ownership.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:To warn others when you have lost control of your vehicle.,b:To greet a friend.,c:To express frustration at other drivers.,d:While passing another car on the highway.
note: Use your horn to warn others of immediate danger, such as when you lose control; avoid using it to express anger or for greetings.

question: If you hit an unattended parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, you should:
options: a:Leave immediately.,b:Wait for the police to arrive before leaving.,c:Leave a written note with your name, address, and accident details.
note: If you cannot locate the owner, leave a written notice with your contact information and a description of the incident in a conspicuous place on the vehicle.

question: A pennant-shaped road sign is used to indicate:
options: a:No passing zones.,b:School zones.,c:Speed limits.
note: Pennant-shaped signs are used to mark no passing zones; the sign's shape and any text confirm the restriction.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light indicate?
options: a:Proceed with caution.,b:Stop like a red light.,c:Pedestrian crossing only.,d:Signal malfunction ahead.
note: A flashing yellow signal warns you to slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution.

question: What is a 'No zone' in relation to large vehicles?
options: a:A designated no-passing zone.,b:A one-way traffic area.,c:The large blind spot around trucks and large vehicles.
note: 'No zones' are the blind spots around large trucks and buses where smaller vehicles disappear from the truck driver's view; avoid lingering there.

question: A single dashed white line separating lanes indicates what?
options: a:This lane is a bicycle-only lane.,b:Drivers may change lanes or pass when safe.,c:Drivers may not pass.,d:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is allowed.
note: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to pass or change lanes when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parallel parking, how many inches from the curb should your wheels be?
options: a:12 inches,b:6 inches,c:18 inches
note: When parallel parked, your wheels should be within six inches of the curb so your vehicle does not obstruct traffic and can be clearly seen.

question: What best describes defensive driving?
options: a:Identifying hazardous situations ahead of time and taking action to avoid crashes.,b:Maintaining a close following distance to control traffic.,c:Trying to outrun poor drivers to stay ahead in traffic.
note: Defensive driving means detecting dangerous driving situations early and taking action to prevent crashes. It reduces conflicts with aggressive, careless, or impaired road users.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless posted otherwise, what is the speed limit in suburban residential districts in New Jersey?
options: a:10 mph.,b:35 mph.,c:45 mph.,d:25 mph.
note: Unless signs indicate otherwise, the default speed limit in suburban residential districts is 35 mph.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless posted otherwise, what is the speed limit in residential districts?
options: a:25 mph.,b:10 mph.,c:45 mph.
note: Unless a different limit is posted, the speed limit in residential districts is 25 miles per hour.

question: What qualifies someone as an inattentive driver?
options: a:Daydreaming or staring at objects off the roadway while driving.,b:Maintaining eye contact with a passenger during conversation.,c:Only watching the vehicle directly ahead.
note: Distracted or inattentive driving includes daydreaming, looking away from the road, or focusing on non-driving tasks instead of scanning the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road, what is required?
options: a:You may use the shoulder as a passing lane.,b:You must cross the centerline (enter the oncoming lane) only when safe and legal.,c:Flash your headlights to force oncoming traffic to yield.
note: On a two-lane two-way road, passing requires entering the oncoming lane; do so only when it is safe and legally permitted.

question: If you are on a two-lane street and a fire engine is following you but it is not using emergency signals, what should you do?
options: a:Continue driving in the normal manner.,b:Stop immediately.,c:Speed up to get out of its way.
note: If an emergency vehicle is not using its lights or siren, you do not need to yield; continue normally unless it activates them.

question: If a transit bus signals to re-enter the traffic lane, how should you react?
options: a:Quickly pass the bus before it re-enters.,b:Yield the right-of-way to the bus.,c:Expect the bus to yield to you.
note: Drivers behind a transit bus should yield space to allow the bus to re-enter traffic safely when it signals.

question: When roads may be slippery, you should:
options: a:Always drive at the posted maximum speed.,b:Use cruise control to maintain speed.,c:Reduce your speed and increase following distance.
note: On slippery surfaces avoid sudden changes in speed or direction, reduce your speed, and increase your following distance; do not use cruise control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which location is specifically listed as a place where passing is prohibited?
options: a:In a tunnel.,b:On a bridge.,c:All of the above (tunnel, bridge, underpass).
note: Drivers should not pass in tunnels, on bridges, or in underpasses. Only pass where it is safe and legal.

question: Which item does vehicle stopping distance not depend on?
options: a:The time of day.,b:Your own reaction time.,c:The condition of your vehicle's brakes.
note: Stopping distance depends on reaction time, vehicle condition, roadway surface, and speed, but not on the time of day by itself.

question: Before starting the engine, what safety step should you do regarding seat belts?
options: a:Make sure you and all passengers have buckled their seat belts.,b:Ensure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.,c:Ensure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
note: Develop a routine: buckle your own safety belt and ensure every passenger is properly buckled before you switch on the ignition.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing without signals, what should you do?
options: a:Always come to a complete stop regardless of whether a train is visible.,b:Assume the crossing has signals and proceed at normal speed.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop; check both directions before crossing.
note: At crossings without signals slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop if necessary.

question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:Human error.,b:New drivers.,c:Bad weather.
note: Most crashes are caused by human error—mistakes in perception, decision, or reaction.

question: On a road with no sidewalks, which direction should a pedestrian walk?
options: a:On the side of the road facing oncoming traffic.,b:On the same side as the traffic is moving.,c:On the side with the lightest traffic.
note: Pedestrians should walk facing oncoming traffic so they can see approaching vehicles and react accordingly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection you should:
options: a:Maintain speed and proceed.,b:Slow down, cover the brake, look left-right-left, and be ready to yield.,c:Yield to all other drivers regardless of position.
note: Approach uncontrolled intersections cautiously: slow, scan all directions, and yield to traffic from the right as necessary to avoid a crash.

question: Which of the following can impair a person's driving ability?
options: a:Any medication.,b:Alcohol.,c:A lack of sleep.
note: Alcohol, many prescription and over-the-counter medications, and fatigue can impair driving; all of these factors reduce safety on the road.

question: In New Jersey, vehicles should not idle for more than:
options: a:Three minutes.,b:Five minutes.,c:Ten minutes.
note: State law generally restricts vehicle idling to three minutes or less except under specific permitted conditions.

question: Hydroplaning is most often caused by which driving behavior?
options: a:Frequent stopping.,b:Sudden turns at low speeds.,c:Driving at excessive speed on wet roads.
note: Hydroplaning occurs when tires cannot clear water because of high speed or poor tire condition, causing loss of traction.

question: Signs warning of hazardous conditions ahead are called what?
options: a:Warning signs.,b:Regulatory signs.,c:Information signs.,d:Guide signs.
note: Warning signs alert drivers to potential hazards ahead and advise caution to avoid accidents.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians?
options: a:Only when the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.,b:Only if the pedestrian is on the same side as the driver.,c:Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway, even if the pedestrian is crossing in a careless or unexpected manner.

question: To reduce headlight glare from oncoming vehicles at night, where should you look?
options: a:Toward the right side of the road ahead.,b:Directly at the oncoming headlights.,c:Over your right shoulder.
note: If oncoming drivers don't dim their lights, focus on the right edge of the roadway to avoid temporary blindness from glare.

question: To avoid remaining in a truck or bus driver's blind spot, you should:
options: a:Avoid driving alongside them and do not tailgate.,b:Never pass large trucks or buses.,c:Flash your headlights to get their attention.
note: Large vehicles have substantial blind spots at their sides and rear; avoid lingering beside them and do not tailgate so the driver can see you.

question: What does a red-and-white triangular sign at an intersection require drivers to do?
options: a:Always come to a full stop.,b:Speed up to clear the intersection.,c:Decrease speed and yield to vehicles and pedestrians; be prepared to stop.,d:Stop only if traffic is heavy.
note: A red-and-white yield sign means slow down, yield the right-of-way to vehicles and pedestrians in or approaching the intersection, and stop if necessary.

question: How does being distracted while driving typically affect a driver's reactions?
options: a:It is never dangerous.,b:It usually causes slower reactions to hazards.,c:It usually causes faster driving.
note: Distracted driving slows reaction times and increases the likelihood of missing hazards or traffic changes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to which of the following?
options: a:Vehicles already circulating in the roundabout.,b:Only pedestrians, not vehicles in the roundabout.,c:Vehicles approaching from behind you.
note: Yield to traffic and bicyclists already in the roundabout, and watch for pedestrians at the entries and exits.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another driver is trying to pass your vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Pull off the road.,b:Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to allow safe passing.,c:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,d:Signal them to stop.
note: Remain in your lane, check for oncoming traffic, and adjust speed so the passing driver can move back into the lane safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop simultaneously, who should yield?
options: a:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.,b:The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.,c:They should make hand signals to decide.
note: If two drivers arrive at the same time, yield to the vehicle on your right; proceed when it is safe.

question: Which practice helps reduce the chance of a rear-end collision?
options: a:Stop quickly to alert drivers behind you.,b:Ignore mirrors before stopping.,c:Avoid sudden stops and release the gas to slow before braking.,d:Brake and then immediately steer sharply.
note: Avoid abrupt stops; release the accelerator to slow, then apply steady braking so your brake lights warn following drivers.

question: When should you look over your shoulder to check the blind spot?
options: a:When changing lanes.,b:When pulling toward or away from a curb.,c:When turning left or right only.
note: Check blind spots by glancing over your shoulder each time you intend to change lanes or move laterally on the road.

question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light, what should you do?
options: a:Proceed through the intersection carefully and with caution.,b:Stop and wait for a green light.,c:Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution, watching for other road users.

question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, you should:
options: a:Flash your lights to warn them.,b:Stay calm and move out of their way.,c:Speed up to follow them.
note: Avoid escalation: stay calm, do not engage, and safely distance yourself from aggressive drivers.

question: At night, which is hardest to see?
options: a:Road signs.,b:Pedestrians.,c:Other motorists.
note: Pedestrians are generally the hardest objects to see at night, so reduce speed and watch for people near the roadway.

question: If you must drive in fog, you should:
options: a:Turn on your low beam headlights.,b:Turn on your hazard lights.,c:Drive at the maximum posted speed.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog to improve visibility; high beams will reflect back and reduce sight distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The space you need to cross traffic safely depends on which factors?
options: a:Road and weather conditions plus oncoming traffic.,b:Presence of a stop sign only.,c:Use of turn signals only.
note: Space needed to cross depends on road and weather conditions and the amount and speed of oncoming traffic.

question: How should a seat belt be worn to provide proper protection?
options: a:Loose and comfortable.,b:Buckled snugly across the hip bones and lower abdomen.,c:Hidden beneath the seat.
note: Lap belts should be snug across the hip bones and lower abdomen and shoulder belts should lie across the chest to reduce injury risk in a crash.

question: Why should you be especially cautious when passing a bicycle?
options: a:Because you are moving faster than the bicycle.,b:The bicycle always has the right-of-way.,c:Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass.
note: Cyclists may need to swerve to avoid hazards and oncoming drivers may not expect you to move into their lane, so pass carefully and give adequate space.

question: If you plan to drink socially, what is a safe strategy to ensure you don't drive impaired?
options: a:Drink coffee before driving.,b:Arrange to ride home with a sober friend.,c:Take a cold shower before driving.,d:Drive slowly to compensate.
note: Riding home with someone who has not been drinking is a safe way to avoid driving while impaired; coffee or showers do not lower BAC.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before making a left turn, what must you do?
options: a:Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.,b:Sound your horn aggressively.,c:Cut the corner to complete the turn quickly.,d:Back into the lane to allow oncoming traffic to pass.
note: When turning left, yield the right-of-way to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians and make the turn only when it is safe.

question: An eight-sided (octagonal) traffic sign always indicates which instruction?
options: a:Speed limit.,b:Stop.,c:Hospital ahead.
note: An octagonal sign always means STOP. Come to a complete stop and proceed only when it is safe.

question: Driving without proper liability insurance coverage may result in:
options: a:No consequences.,b:A warning only.,c:Fines and other penalties.
note: Operating a vehicle without required liability insurance can lead to fines, license and registration suspension, and other penalties.

question: Who must wear a seat belt in a moving passenger vehicle?
options: a:The driver and all passengers must wear seat belts.,b:Only the driver must wear a seat belt.,c:Only child passengers must wear seat belts.
note: State law requires the driver and all passengers to wear seat belts; the driver is responsible for passengers under 18.

question: When must you stop for a school bus on a two-lane highway?
options: a:When you are driving on a two-lane highway and the bus's red lights are flashing.,b:When the bus is parked on the shoulder and empty.,c:Only when the bus displays a stop sign arm.
note: On two-lane roads, traffic from both directions must stop when a school bus is stopped with red lights flashing and the stop arm extended.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you legally cross double solid yellow lines?
options: a:To turn into a driveway or to make a permitted left turn.,b:To pass a slow-moving car.,c:To pass at any time roadway is clear.
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing, but you may cross them to turn left into a driveway or designated lane where permitted.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal indicates that which light will appear next?
options: a:Steady red.,b:Flashing yellow.,c:Steady green.
note: A steady yellow means the signal is about to change to a steady red; prepare to stop if you can do so safely.

question: At a light rail or train track intersection, what should you always do?
options: a:Obey all signals, look both ways, and never go around lowered gates.,b:Assume trains yield to cars.,c:Rely only on flashing lights to warn you of trains.
note: Always look both ways, obey signals and gates, and never drive around lowered crossing gates or ignore warning devices.

question: What does a pentagonal (five-sided) sign usually indicate?
options: a:Speed limits.,b:School zone or school crossing.,c:No passing zones.,d:Pedestrian crossing ahead.
note: Pentagonal signs indicate you are in an area used by schools—be extra alert for children and pedestrians nearby.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit represent?
options: a:The maximum or minimum legal speed under ideal conditions.,b:Only a recommended speed.,c:The exact speed you must travel to avoid a ticket regardless of conditions.
note: A posted speed limit indicates the maximum (and sometimes minimum) legal speed under ideal conditions. Drive slower when conditions are hazardous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a narrow road when you meet an oncoming vehicle, what must you do?
options: a:Pull completely off the road every time.,b:Demand the other vehicle pull over.,c:Speed up and pass quickly.,d:Allow at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road to the oncoming vehicle.
note: On narrow roads, give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the traveled portion so both can pass safely.

question: When merging onto a freeway, what is the safest approach?
options: a:Accelerate on the ramp to match freeway traffic speed.,b:Proceed very slowly until you find a gap.,c:Turn on hazard lights until fully merged.,d:Stop at the end of the ramp then enter traffic when clear.
note: Use the on-ramp to accelerate to the speed of freeway traffic so you can safely merge; traffic on the freeway has the right-of-way.

question: If you hear a siren but cannot immediately locate the emergency vehicle, what is the correct action?
options: a:Slow down but do not stop until you can see the vehicle.,b:Keep driving until you see the emergency vehicle, then pull over.,c:Safely pull to the right side of the road and stop until you are sure the vehicle is not headed toward you.
note: If you hear an emergency vehicle nearby and do not know its exact direction, pull over to the right and stop to allow it to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:When driving so slowly that it disrupts the normal flow of traffic.,b:When in heavy traffic in a construction zone.,c:Only when driving in rural areas.
note: It is unlawful to drive so slowly that you impede the normal flow of traffic unless conditions require it for safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are on the interstate and miss your exit, what is the correct action?
options: a:Continue driving and use the next exit.,b:Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.,c:Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
note: Do not make last-minute turns or dangerous maneuvers if you pass an exit; proceed to the next exit and re-route from there.

question: What must you do when a school bus is stopped with its stop arm extended?
options: a:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the stop arm is withdrawn.,b:Honk before passing cautiously.,c:Pass on the right if no children are visible.,d:Proceed if you are in a different lane on a multilane road.
note: When a school bus displays its stop signal, all drivers approaching in either direction must stop until the bus resumes motion and the signal is withdrawn.

question: On a divided multilane highway, if you hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Disregard the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.,b:Stop as quickly as possible in your lane.,c:Slow down, move your vehicle to provide a clear path, and stop.
note: Provide a clear path by pulling to the right and stopping when necessary to allow the emergency vehicle to pass safely.

question: A leaky exhaust system can cause which of the following hazards to occupants?
options: a:Loss of vehicle power only.,b:Immediate tire failure.,c:Carbon monoxide poisoning.
note: Exhaust leaks can allow carbon monoxide into the passenger area; this odorless gas is life-threatening—repair leaks promptly.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing that has no flashing lights or gates, you should:
options: a:Cross immediately and quickly.,b:Always stop before crossing.,c:Be prepared to yield to any train at the crossing.
note: At crossings without active controls, look and listen for trains and be prepared to yield; never enter unless there is room to clear the tracks on the far side.

question: If a vehicle with ABS begins to lose traction, what should the driver do with the brake pedal?
options: a:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.,b:Pump the brakes manually.,c:Press and hold the accelerator.
note: With ABS, press down hard on the brake pedal and hold it while steering to safety; the system will automatically modulate braking.

question: When must headlights be used?
options: a:One half hour before sunrise.,b:One half hour after sunset.,c:Only when parked at a school.
note: Headlights are required from one half hour after sunset until one half hour before sunrise, when visibility is under 500 feet, and whenever windshield wipers are in use due to rain or snow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn, where should your vehicle be positioned?
options: a:Near the center of the street.,b:Close to the left side of the street.,c:As close to the right side of the street as possible.
note: When preparing to make a right turn, move as far to the right as practicable; do not swing wide into other lanes.

question: As alcohol accumulates in your blood, what effects occur?
options: a:Immediate sober clarity.,b:Reduced error-making skills.,c:Slowed reactions, impaired judgment, and increased confidence despite decreased ability.,d:Faster reflexes and better memory.
note: Alcohol slows reaction time, impairs judgment and perception, and can falsely increase confidence while degrading driving skills.

question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, what should you do?
options: a:Retaliate by tailgating.,b:Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.,c:Make obscene gestures to show displeasure.
note: Stay calm, avoid eye contact, get out of their way, and allow them to pass to reduce the risk of escalation.

question: At an intersection with a flashing red light, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a full stop and go when safe.,b:Stop only if other cars are approaching.,c:Stop only if other cars are already inside the intersection.
note: A flashing red light has the same meaning as a stop sign: stop completely, yield as required, and proceed when safe.

question: To check a blind spot before changing lanes, you should:
options: a:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.,b:Rely solely on the side mirror.,c:Only glance at the rearview mirror.
note: A quick over-the-shoulder glance in the direction you intend to move will reveal vehicles in blind spots that mirrors miss.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How far in advance should you signal before beginning a turn?
options: a:20 feet.,b:50 feet.,c:100 feet.
note: Signal at least 100 feet before you turn to adequately warn other drivers and pedestrians of your intentions.

question: What does the Implied Consent Law require of New Jersey drivers?
options: a:To grant permission to someone else to drive your vehicle.,b:To wear safety belts at all times.,c:To submit to a breath test if suspected of driving under the influence.
note: By driving on New Jersey roads you implicitly consent to a breath test when arrested on suspicion of alcohol-related driving offenses.

question: What is the safest way to cross a railroad track?
options: a:Cross quickly when you see a train far away.,b:Look and listen both ways, and proceed only when it is safe.,c:Drive around lowered gates if no train is visible.,d:Rely only on signals without looking.
note: Always look and listen for trains before crossing; obey gates and signals and never go around lowered barriers.

question: Does drinking coffee after consuming alcohol lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:It lowers BAC.,b:It cancels the effect of alcohol.,c:It has no effect on BAC.
note: Only time reduces BAC. Coffee, exercise, or cold showers may make you more alert but do not reduce your blood alcohol level.

question: At dusk or on overcast days you should:
options: a:Drive using your four-way flashers.,b:Turn on your headlights (low beam) to increase visibility.,c:Not use any vehicle lights.
note: Turn on your headlights in low-light conditions such as dusk or overcast days; use low beams within 1,000 feet of oncoming vehicles and 500 feet of following vehicles.

question: Which restriction applies to drivers under 21 with a probationary license?
options: a:May use a hands-free cellphone while driving.,b:May not drive between 11:01 p.m. and 5:00 a.m.,c:Should not wear a seat belt while driving.
note: Probationary license holders under 21 must follow GDL restrictions, including a curfew (11:01 p.m. to 5:00 a.m.), and are prohibited from using hand-held or hands-free phones; seat belts are required.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is signaling before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb required?
options: a:Only necessary if other traffic is present.,b:Required by law and a good driving habit.,c:Only necessary during the maneuver, not before.
note: Signaling is required by law (typically at least 100 feet before a turn) and is essential to inform others of your intentions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on an interstate, you should:
options: a:Stop and make a U-turn on the highway.,b:Get off at the next exit and return to your destination safely.,c:Back up in the lane to reach the exit.
note: Do not back up or make illegal turns on the highway; proceed to the next exit and safely return to your planned route.

question: What lane width is a motorcycle entitled to use?
options: a:The bicycle lane only.,b:The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.,c:Half the width of a standard lane.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the full width of a traffic lane just like other motor vehicles.

question: Where should you maintain a cushion of space around your vehicle?
options: a:Only behind your vehicle.,b:Only on the left and right sides.,c:On all sides of the vehicle.
note: To give yourself time to react to hazards, keep a space cushion on all sides of your vehicle; do not crowd other vehicles.

question: What does a green arrow displayed on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Used only on one-way streets.,b:It has the same meaning as a circular green light but traffic must turn in the arrow's direction.,c:You may proceed only if a circular green light is also on.
note: A green arrow indicates that traffic in the lane controlled by the arrow may proceed in the direction shown; yield to pedestrians and other traffic as required.

question: How can road rage and aggressive driving be reduced?
options: a:Allow extra travel time, obey speed limits, and use proper signals.,b:Drive faster to get clear of congestion.,c:Ignore other drivers entirely while driving.
note: Plan ahead, obey limits, and signal properly to reduce stress and avoid provoking or being provoked by aggressive drivers.

question: If you are under 21 and hold a GDL permit, how long must you practice supervised driving before taking the road test?
options: a:Three months,b:Six months,c:One month
note: Drivers under age 21 with a GDL permit must complete at least six months of supervised driving before the road test (drivers 21+ require a shorter period).

question: When involved in a crash, which of these should a driver do first?
options: a:Stop the vehicle at or near the scene.,b:Turn off the ignitions of wrecked vehicles first.,c:Stand in a traffic lane to direct traffic.
note: If involved in an accident, stop at or near the scene, move vehicles out of traffic if possible, and avoid standing in traffic lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you approach a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights on the roadside, what must you do?
options: a:Honk to alert the emergency workers.,b:Maintain speed and position in your lane.,c:Stop immediately in your lane next to the emergency vehicle.,d:Move over to another lane if possible, or slow down if you cannot.
note: You must change lanes away from stopped emergency or road service vehicles when it is safe, or slow down well below the posted limit if you cannot change lanes.

question: Signs that require drivers to obey an indicated instruction are called:
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Warning signs.,c:Information signs.
note: Regulatory signs inform drivers of traffic laws and regulations; failing to obey them may result in penalties.

question: If you are involved in a serious crash, what should you do first?
options: a:Stop and, if possible, move the vehicle off the road; check for injuries and call 911.,b:Leave the scene and report it later.,c:Drive away if damage is minor.,d:Wait in your car without checking for injuries.
note: Stop your vehicle, move to safety if possible, check for injuries, and call emergency services; report the crash if required by law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are turning left onto a one-way street, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:The rightmost lane.,b:The farthest lane from your previous lane.,c:Either lane at random.,d:The lane closest to your previous lane.
note: Turn into the lane that is nearest to the lane you came from on the one-way street, not into the right lane unless that is the closest.

question: Which driving habit can help conserve gasoline?
options: a:Accelerating quickly from stops.,b:Sitting idling in driveways.,c:Slowing down gradually and avoiding abrupt stops.
note: Smooth driving—anticipating traffic and slowing gradually rather than braking hard—improves fuel efficiency.

question: When during a rainstorm are roads most slippery and hazardous?
options: a:During the first 10 to 15 minutes of the rain.,b:The day after it rains.,c:When it has been raining steadily for hours.
note: Oil and residue on the pavement come to the surface in the first minutes of rain, making the road especially slippery.

question: If your wheels drop onto the shoulder, what should you do to re-enter the pavement?
options: a:Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.,b:Stop on the edge of the road.,c:Slow down, regain control, and carefully steer back onto the pavement.
note: Reduce speed without braking hard, check for traffic, and carefully steer back onto the roadway to avoid losing control.

question: Where is parking expressly prohibited among these choices?
options: a:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.,b:On a hill.,c:In a parking lot.
note: It is unlawful to park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane; when parking on-street, you must be within 12 inches of the curb.

question: What is the shape of a standard stop sign?
options: a:A circle.,b:An octagon.,c:A rectangle.
note: Stop signs are the only standard traffic signs with an octagonal shape and require drivers to come to a complete stop.

question: A solid white line between lanes of traffic means:
options: a:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.,c:Lanes move in the same direction and lane changes are discouraged (no passing).
note: Solid white lines separate lanes of traffic going in the same direction and discourage lane changes; passing across a solid white line is generally not permitted.

question: What do your brake lights tell other road users?
options: a:You are changing gears.,b:You are about to switch lanes.,c:You are stopping or slowing down.,d:You are turning right.
note: Brake lights signal to drivers behind you that you are slowing down or stopping; they must be kept in working order.

question: When meeting an oncoming vehicle at night, your headlights should be:
options: a:Set on high beam.,b:Set on low beam.,c:Turned off and use parking lights only.
note: Use low-beam headlights when approaching or following other vehicles to avoid blinding other drivers.

question: What must drivers under 21 with a probationary license display on their license plates?
options: a:Four GDL decals.,b:Two GDL decals.,c:Two flashing lights.
note: Drivers under 21 with a probationary license must display two visible, reflective GDL decals on their license plates provided by the MVC.

question: The single most effective action to reduce your risk of injury or death in a crash is to:
options: a:Always stay in the right lane.,b:Limit driving to weekdays.,c:Always wear your seat belt.
note: Wearing a seat belt is the most effective measure to reduce the risk of serious injury or death in a crash.

question: MVC may refuse to begin your road test if:
options: a:You brought an unsafe test vehicle.,b:A center console or vehicle equipment blocks the examiner's access to the foot brake.,c:Your vehicle has a working horn.
note: The examiner must be able to reach the foot brake and parking brake; vehicles missing required equipment or obstructing examiner access may be refused.

question: What does a single broken white line between lanes indicate?
options: a:Lanes are reserved for buses only.,b:Lanes move in the same direction and passing or lane changes are permitted.,c:Lanes move in the same direction and passing is prohibited.,d:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is permitted.
note: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction; drivers may change lanes or pass if it is safe to do so.

question: If you experience a tire blowout, what sequence of actions is recommended?
options: a:Gradually slow down, take your foot off the gas, and pull off the side of the road when safe.,b:Immediately slam on the brakes and stop in the travel lane.,c:Speed up and steer to the shoulder quickly.
note: Do not brake suddenly; reduce speed gradually, steer to a safe area, and then stop to inspect the tire.

question: What should you do when changing lanes on a highway?
options: a:Signal your lane change.,b:Check your rearview and outside mirrors.,c:Do all of the above (signal, check mirrors, and check your blind spot).
note: Before changing lanes signal, check all mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot; do not rely on mirrors alone.

question: What color lines divide lanes of traffic moving in the same direction?
options: a:Red.,b:Yellow.,c:White.
note: Solid or broken white lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction; yellow lines separate opposing traffic.

question: Which of these winter-driving statements is NOT true?
options: a:Winter is the most difficult driving season.,b:Checking antifreeze and washer fluid is important in winter.,c:Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
note: Do not use cruise control on snow or ice; winter driving requires extra caution and monitoring of vehicle fluids and systems.

question: What is true about advisory speed or curve warning signs?
options: a:They may be ignored in rainy conditions.,b:They are triangular in shape.,c:You should reduce speed in adverse conditions regardless of the posted advisory.
note: Advisory speeds and warning signs suggest safe speeds for conditions; in rain, snow, or ice you should reduce speed below the advisory as needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where you and a vehicle on your right arrive simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:You should speed up to get through first.,b:Yield to the vehicle on your right.,c:Enter the intersection and make the other vehicle stop.
note: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your right.

question: How should you respond when you see other drivers acting angrily or aggressively?
options: a:Make eye contact to show you won't be intimidated.,b:React with hand gestures.,c:Distance yourself from the situation and avoid eye contact or gestures.,d:Speed up and engage them.
note: Avoid interacting with aggressive drivers; slow down, move over, and put distance between you and them to reduce risk.

question: On slippery roads, what is the safest action?
options: a:Slow down.,b:Drive faster to avoid skidding.,c:Maintain the posted speed limit regardless of conditions.
note: When rain, snow, or sleet make roads slippery, reduce your speed below the posted limit if needed to maintain control.

question: How can you avoid alcohol-related driving risks?
options: a:Tell others you are driving after you've started drinking.,b:Only drink beer instead of spirits.,c:Decide before you begin drinking that you will not drive and make other transportation plans.
note: The surest way to avoid impaired driving is to plan not to drive before you begin drinking and arrange a sober ride.

question: What can happen when alcohol is consumed with drugs?
options: a:Decrease the effects of drugs and alcohol.,b:Increase the effects of both and worsen impairment.,c:Neutralize alcohol in the bloodstream.,d:Cure side effects of medications.
note: Mixing alcohol and drugs can amplify their effects and make driving even more dangerous.

question: How should drivers respond to a flashing yellow traffic signal?
options: a:Increase their speed.,b:Come to a complete stop.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light warns of a hazard ahead. Slow down and proceed carefully; it does not require a full stop.

question: Why is a leaking exhaust system dangerous?
options: a:It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning, which can make you drowsy or cause death.,b:It mainly causes your vehicle to use more oil.,c:It only increases noise levels.
note: A leaking exhaust can allow toxic gases like carbon monoxide into the cabin, causing dizziness, drowsiness, or death; repair leaks immediately.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are required to stop your vehicle in which of the following situations?
options: a:At an intersection with a stop sign.,b:Only where a police officer orders it.,c:Only when a red light is flashing.
note: You must stop at stop signs, where a traffic officer directs you to stop, and at red or flashing red lights controlling an intersection.

question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, what must drivers do?
options: a:Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.,b:Follow whatever surrounding traffic does, ignoring the guard.,c:Assume the guard is not supposed to direct traffic.
note: Always obey crossing guards and be prepared to reduce speed and stop when directed in school zones.

question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, what should you do next?
options: a:Watch carefully for children walking along the side of the road before proceeding.,b:Drive immediately once the bus door closes.,c:Do not proceed until a child waves to you.
note: After a bus with flashing red lights and an extended stop arm stops, watch for children near the roadway and proceed only when safe.

question: A yellow-and-black diamond-shaped sign typically serves what purpose?
options: a:It warns of conditions on or near the road ahead.,b:It provides directions to towns and cities.,c:It tells you specific traffic laws and regulations.
note: Diamond-shaped yellow signs warn of upcoming hazards or changes in the road ahead.

question: On a highway marked with double solid yellow lines, you may:
options: a:Cross only to make a left turn into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.,b:Cross to pass slower vehicles if no oncoming traffic is present.,c:Never cross under any circumstance.
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing; you may cross them only to make lawful left turns into or from driveways, alleys, or private roads.

question: How should you treat a motorcycle traveling near you?
options: a:Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.,b:Allow the motorcycle to use a full traffic lane.,c:Allow the motorcycle to use only half of a lane.
note: A motorcycle is a full-size vehicle with the same rights to a full lane. Give motorcyclists the full lane width for safety and maneuvering.

question: If you are upset or angry before driving, what should you do?
options: a:Play loud music to distract yourself.,b:Drive fast to let off steam.,c:Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.
note: If emotionally upset, cool off before driving. Driving while angry or distracted is dangerous and impairs judgment.

question: When sharing the road with trucks, remember that trucks usually:
options: a:Require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.,b:Can stop more quickly than passenger cars.,c:Have a smaller turning radius than cars.
note: Large trucks require greater stopping distance and need more room to maneuver, so afford them extra space.

question: Under New Jersey's Child Passenger Safety Law, children under eight years old who are shorter than which height must be in an approved safety seat or booster?
options: a:5 feet 5 inches,b:5 feet,c:4 feet 11 inches.
note: Children under age eight and under the height specified by law must be properly restrained in an approved car seat or booster in the rear seat; the law's height threshold is under 4'9\."

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following must you obey over traffic lights and signs?
options: a:A steady red light.,b:A police officer directing traffic.,c:A stop sign.
note: Directions from authorized traffic officers take precedence over signs, signals, and pavement markings.

question: When children ride in vehicles, which statement is correct?
options: a:They may be safely held by a strong adult.,b:They are safe standing on the floor in the back of the vehicle.,c:Children must be properly secured in an appropriate child restraint.
note: Children must be secured in proper child safety seats or seat belts appropriate to their size and age; holding them in arms is unsafe in a crash.

question: When preparing to change lanes, which actions should you take?
options: a:Quickly turn your head without checking mirrors.,b:Check side and rearview mirrors and then glance over your shoulder.,c:Only check your side mirror.,d:Sound your horn before changing lanes.
note: Before changing lanes, check your side and rearview mirrors for approaching traffic and briefly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with flashing signals, how far must you stop from the nearest rail?
options: a:At least 15 feet if warning devices are active.,b:No more than 5 feet.,c:Anywhere within the crossing area.
note: If warning lights or gates are active you must stop no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail and wait for the train to pass and warnings to clear.

question: When driving to an unfamiliar area, you should:
options: a:Depend solely on road signs.,b:Plan your trip in advance.,c:Drive with only a general idea of your destination.
note: Plan your route before you go, and use maps or GPS to avoid last-minute lane changes and unsafe maneuvers.

question: What does a steady green light at an intersection allow you to do?
options: a:Prepare to stop.,b:Stop and check for oncoming traffic.,c:Drive through the intersection if it is clear.
note: A steady green light means you may proceed through the intersection if it is clear; yield to pedestrians and other traffic as necessary.

question: If you are driving behind a school bus with flashing red lights, what must you do?
options: a:Stop at least 25 feet away.,b:Slow to 10 mph.,c:Speed up and pass the bus.
note: When a school bus displays flashing red lights, stop at least 25 feet away. An exception exists for opposite sides of a divided highway.

question: During the probationary period after a special learner permit, how many points against your license will require Probationary Driver Program enrollment?
options: a:Four points.,b:Three points.,c:Two points.
note: A new driver may not be convicted of two or more moving violations totaling four or more points during the two-year period without being required to enroll in the Probationary Driver Program.

question: Which action helps prevent carbon monoxide poisoning from vehicle exhaust?
options: a:Have the exhaust system checked regularly for leaks.,b:Keep the engine running in an enclosed garage.,c:Close vents while following another car closely.
note: Have your exhaust system inspected regularly and avoid running the engine in enclosed spaces. Carbon monoxide is odorless and can be deadly.

question: For normal driving, where should you place your hands on the steering wheel?
options: a:At 1 and 11 o'clock.,b:At 2 and 10 o'clock.,c:At the 3 and 9 o'clock positions.
note: Think of the wheel as a clock face; the recommended hand positions for normal driving are 3 and 9 o'clock, keeping thumbs along the wheel face.

question: How would you describe distracted driving?
options: a:Not a serious concern.,b:Extremely risky behavior that endangers everyone.,c:Very uncommon.
note: Distracted driving is a dangerous behavior that significantly increases the risk of crashes for drivers and others on the road.

question: Why must you use extra caution when driving at night?
options: a:There is a larger volume of traffic at night.,b:Traffic moves faster at night.,c:Drivers cannot see as well at night as they can during the day.
note: Reduced visibility at night makes it harder to see hazards; use headlights and reduce speed accordingly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must a driver do when approaching a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Increase speed to clear the intersection.,b:Merge to the right and continue.,c:Slow down without stopping.,d:Stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.
note: A flashing red light requires a complete stop; yield as necessary and proceed only when it is safe.

question: Under ideal driving conditions, what is the minimum safe following distance?
options: a:Three seconds.,b:One second.,c:Two seconds.
note: Use the Three-Second-Plus rule: pick a fixed object, and if you pass it three seconds after the vehicle ahead did, you have a safe following distance under ideal conditions.

question: What should a driver do if they are taking an over-the-counter medication?
options: a:Drink alcohol instead.,b:Read the drug label for warnings about driving.,c:Ignore any warning labels and drive normally.
note: Many nonprescription medicines can impair driving. Read labels and consult a doctor/pharmacist if unsure about driving while using a medication.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to other drivers while entering traffic?
options: a:Only when you are turning left on a main road.,b:When entering a street from a garage, alley, or driveway.,c:Only when your traffic signal is a green arrow.
note: Yield to traffic and pedestrians when entering a street from a garage, alley, or driveway.

question: Regulatory road signs primarily do what?
options: a:Warn of present dangers.,b:Indicate laws and rules drivers must follow.,c:Are diamond-shaped and yellow.,d:Provide destination distances.
note: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must or must not do in that area (e.g., speed limits, no turns).

question: To drive safely at night, you should:
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Always avoid driving when tired.,c:Make sure your headlights and taillights are working properly.
note: At night reduce speed, increase following distance, avoid driving while fatigued, and ensure your lights are in good condition.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes going your direction, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:Always into the middle lane.,b:Always into the far left lane.,c:Into the lane closest to the lane you came from.,d:Into any lane you choose then change lanes immediately.
note: Turn into the lane nearest your original lane and do not change lanes until the turn is completed and it is safe.

question: When must you yield the right-of-way to an emergency vehicle?
options: a:When you see its flashing lights or hear its siren.,b:Only when it is directly behind you.,c:Only if other drivers yield first.
note: You must yield to emergency vehicles that are using lights and/or sirens by pulling to the right and stopping when necessary.

question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, what should drivers do?
options: a:Assume the flagger is unnecessary and proceed.,b:Follow what other drivers are doing instead.,c:Speed up to clear the zone quickly.,d:Follow the flagger's directions.
note: Always obey directions from flaggers, signs, or officers in work zones—ignoring them is dangerous and illegal.

question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, how must you respond?
options: a:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.,b:Slow down but stay in your lane.,c:Turn on hazard lights and continue at the same speed.,d:Speed up to get out of the way quickly.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with sirens, pull to the curb or side of the road and stop to allow it to pass.

question: Approaching a crossing with a crossbuck but no gates or lights, how should you proceed?
options: a:Approach cautiously and cross only after confirming no trains are coming.,b:Turn the radio down to listen for a train.,c:Proceed only if a flagger signals you to go.
note: At crossings without active signals, always look in both directions and cross only when you are certain no train is approaching.

question: In which situations is it important to reduce your speed?
options: a:On narrow/winding roads, intersections or railroad crossings, and wet or slippery roads.,b:Only in heavy traffic.,c:Only when you see a police car.,d:Never reduce speed unless required by a sign.
note: Reduce speed in narrow or winding sections, near intersections and crossings, and when roads are wet or slippery for safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, what is the proper response?
options: a:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,b:Maintain the same speed.,c:Slow down to create space in front of your vehicle for the other driver to pass.
note: Slow slightly to give passing motorists enough room to complete the maneuver safely and quickly.

question: If your power steering fails while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Work hard to steer, reduce speed, drive to a safe area, and stop.,b:Honk your horn and turn off the ignition immediately.,c:Turn on hazard lights and brace yourself.
note: Power steering loss requires more steering effort; slow down and pull off to a safe location to stop and assess the problem.

question: If your vehicle lacks ABS and you must stop quickly in an emergency, what braking method should you use?
options: a:Firmly pump the brakes to stop while maintaining steering control.,b:Hold down the brake pedal continuously.,c:Lightly tap the brakes repeatedly.
note: If you don't have ABS, pumping the brakes helps you stop quickly and maintain steering control.

question: When should you allow extra space in front of your vehicle when stopped?
options: a:When stopped at an intersection.,b:When stopped at a stop sign.,c:When stopped on an uphill incline.
note: Allow a larger space cushion when stopped on an uphill slope. If the vehicle in front rolls back when traffic resumes, extra space reduces the chance of a collision.

question: What is a safe strategy for driving through a curve?
options: a:Slow down before entering and accelerate gradually as you exit.,b:Maintain constant speed through the curve.,c:Speed up before entering and brake in the curve.,d:Turn the wheel sharply mid-curve.
note: Reduce speed before the curve, then gently increase speed as you exit to maintain control and traction.

question: When passing a large vehicle such as a truck, what should smaller vehicle drivers be prepared for?
options: a:Wind gusts that may affect your steering.,b:Loud music from the truck.,c:Decreased fuel efficiency.,d:Reduced noise levels.
note: Large vehicles can create significant air turbulence or wind gusts that may push smaller vehicles—be ready to correct steering as needed.

question: If you turn onto a two-lane road that is divided by a broken yellow line, you immediately know that:
options: a:Traffic moves in both directions on that road.,b:You are on a one-way road.,c:The road is temporarily under repair.
note: A yellow centerline separates opposing traffic; a broken yellow line means crossing is permitted to pass when safe.

question: When you see a blind pedestrian using a white cane or a guide dog, you should:
options: a:Proceed normally as they must yield.,b:Honk to alert them.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop.
note: Yield to blind pedestrians, stop if necessary, and proceed only when it is safe; do not assume they can see or hear you.

question: Which is true about drivers holding a probationary license?
options: a:They may use a hand-held cell phone while driving.,b:They must wear a seat belt though their passengers are exempt.,c:They may not use a hands-free cell phone while driving.
note: Probationary drivers are subject to restrictions: they must wear seat belts and are prohibited from using hand-held or often any phone devices while driving.

question: If an aggressive driver is following you or driving aggressively, you should:
options: a:Stare at the driver as they pass.,b:Try to get out of their way and avoid escalation.,c:Speed up to keep ahead of them.
note: Avoid confrontation: slow down or move over when safe to allow the aggressive driver to pass and report dangerous behavior if needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you slow down while exiting a highway?
options: a:On the main road just before the exit lane.,b:Only when you see a toll booth ahead.,c:After you have moved into the exit lane.
note: Do not begin to reduce speed until after you have moved into the exit lane; plan ahead and get into the exit lane in advance.

question: If you are upset, anxious, or crying before driving, what should you do?
options: a:Take time to calm down and focus on driving before starting the engine.,b:Assume you will drive no differently than usual.,c:Drive faster because you feel more alert.
note: Emotional distractions reduce driving ability; take time to calm and focus before operating a vehicle.

question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, the first step is to:
options: a:Firmly apply your brakes.,b:Take your foot off the gas pedal.,c:Apply the parking brake.
note: On slippery surfaces first ease off the gas to reduce speed; apply brakes gently if more slowing is needed to avoid locking wheels.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about speed is true?
options: a:Driving too slowly can be dangerous in some situations.,b:Speeding is not harmful if you are an experienced driver.,c:Speed has no effect on crash severity.,d:Higher speed reduces stopping distance.
note: Both excessive speed and driving much slower than traffic can be dangerous; higher speeds greatly increase the chance of fatalities.

question: When parking uphill next to a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Keep the rear tires against the curb.,b:Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.,c:Keep the front tires straight ahead.
note: Facing uphill with a curb, turn the wheels away so that if the vehicle rolls it will settle against the curb and stop.

question: Which of these is NOT a factor affecting blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:How much time passes between drinks.,b:Your body weight.,c:The type of alcoholic beverage consumed.
note: BAC is influenced by amount consumed, body weight, and time between drinks. The specific type of beverage (beer, wine, liquor) does not change the amount of alcohol absorbed.

question: If you are driving in another vehicle's blind spot, you should:
options: a:Flash your lights to alert the other driver.,b:Move forward or fall back so the other driver can see you.,c:Maintain a steady position in that blind spot.
note: Do not remain in another driver's blind spot; move forward or slow down to drop back so you are visible.

question: When approaching a heavy truck from behind while driving uphill, what should you expect?
options: a:The truck may be traveling slower than the posted limit and you may not be able to safely pass on the hill.,b:The truck will always be at or above the speed limit.,c:You may legally pass if you have enough speed.,d:The truck must pull over to let you pass.
note: Large trucks often slow on inclines; on hills with limited visibility or where it is unsafe, you may not be able or permitted to pass.

question: If one of your tires blows out while driving, how should you react?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the gas, steer straight, then brake gently and pull off safely.,b:Apply the brakes hard immediately.,c:Keep your speed and maintain the course until you reach a service station.
note: Keep control, do not brake suddenly, steer straight, slow gradually, then pull safely off the roadway and stop.

question: What should you remember about wet pavement conditions?
options: a:Roads are especially slippery right after it starts to rain.,b:Wet roads can cause hydroplaning.,c:Give yourself additional stopping distance (all of the above).
note: Wet roads are often most slippery just after rain begins due to surface film; reduce speed and increase following distance to lower crash risk.

question: Which of the following is true about seat belts and child restraints?
options: a:Never place a rear-facing infant restraint in a front seat with an active airbag.,b:An airbag is safe for infants in any restraint.,c:Seat belts are optional for adult passengers.
note: Infants and small children should be properly restrained in rear seats; never place a rear-facing infant seat in front of an active passenger airbag.

question: How should you check your vehicle's blind spots?
options: a:Turn your head and look over your shoulder into the blind spot.,b:Rely only on your side mirrors.,c:Check only the rearview mirror.
note: Blind spots are areas your mirrors cannot show. Look over your shoulder in the direction you intend to move to check them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left, what steps should you take?
options: a:Turn sharply from any lane.,b:Ignore rearview mirrors.,c:Signal early, slow gradually, move into the left lane if required, and watch for vehicles and pedestrians.,d:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
note: Signal three to five seconds in advance, check mirrors, move into the proper lane, yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic, and complete the turn when safe.

question: Before changing lanes, how should you check blind spots?
options: a:Turn your head to look over your shoulder to check blind spots, in addition to using mirrors.,b:Only use the inside rearview mirror.,c:Only use the outside mirrors.
note: Always turn your head and check blind spots before changing lanes; mirrors alone may not reveal all hazards.
