question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:
options: a:Directed to do so by a flagger.,b:It is controlled by a stop sign.,c:Flashing red signals and gates are operating.
note: Stop for railroad crossings when signs or flaggers order you to stop, when gates are down, or when lights are flashing.

question: “Highway hypnosis” is a condition that can result from:
options: a:Too much sleep the night before.,b:Staring at the roadway for long periods.,c:Frequent rest stops.
note: Highway hypnosis can cause a driver to zone out after long periods of monotony; stay alert by taking breaks and scanning the road.

question: Road patches that are shaded by trees or buildings are dangerous because:
options: a:They freeze more quickly and are the last to dry, creating icy spots.,b:They are always clear of debris.,c:They remain warm longer than open areas.
note: Shaded areas can remain icy or wet longer than sunny sections and require extra caution in cold or wet weather.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do if you approach an intersection blocked by traffic ahead?
options: a:Stay out of the intersection until you can completely clear it.,b:Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.,c:Proceed slowly until traffic ahead moves.
note: Do not enter an intersection you cannot clear; block intersections create hazards for cross traffic and pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn, what should you avoid doing?
options: a:Signaling in advance.,b:Cutting corners.,c:Slowing down.,d:Yielding to pedestrians.
note: Do not cut corners when turning left; begin slowing and signal before making the turn to avoid interfering with other vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You cannot safely pass on a two-way, two-lane road unless:
options: a:You can clearly see the road ahead and can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.,b:You are able to exceed the speed limit to complete the pass.,c:You are driving a vehicle capable of high speeds.
note: Only pass on two-way roads when you have a clear view ahead, enough space to return to your lane before oncoming traffic, and it is legal and safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless posted otherwise, what is the speed limit in business districts?
options: a:70 mph.,b:25 mph.,c:40 mph.,d:55 mph.
note: Unless signs indicate another speed, the standard speed limit in business districts is 25 mph.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a congested freeway you should:
options: a:Yield to traffic already on the freeway.,b:Use the acceleration lane to adjust your speed to match freeway traffic.,c:Check your side and rearview mirrors and your blind spot before merging.
note: Use the entrance (acceleration) lane to reach the speed of freeway traffic, yield to vehicles already on the freeway, and use mirrors and blind-spot checks to merge safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When the centerline shows a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line and the broken line is next to your lane, when may you pass?
options: a:Only on expressways.,b:You may pass if oncoming traffic is clear.,c:Only in an emergency.
note: If the broken line is on your side of the centerline, you may cross it to pass when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, how should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Leave wheels pointed straight ahead.,b:Turn wheels into traffic.,c:Turn your wheels toward the curb (to the right).,d:Turn your wheels to the left.
note: On a downhill slope, turn your wheels toward the curb so that if the vehicle rolls, it will roll away from traffic.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic signal mean?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop and wait for green.,c:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
note: A flashing yellow light warns you to slow down and proceed carefully through the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are stopped in a line at a stop sign and there is no cross traffic after cars ahead have gone, what must you do?
options: a:Proceed without stopping again.,b:Stop again at the stop sign or stop line before proceeding.,c:Slowly roll past the stop sign if clear.
note: You must bring your vehicle to a complete stop at the stop sign or line each time, even if cars ahead have already cleared the intersection.

question: Can you go around or under a railroad crossing gate that is moving?
options: a:Only if an approaching train is not too close.,b:If doing so will not damage the gate.,c:No, you must not go around or under a lowering or lowered gate.
note: Never drive around or under crossing gates; wait until lights stop flashing and gates are fully raised before crossing.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is nearby, you should:
options: a:Stop immediately and block their path.,b:Speed up to get out of the way.,c:Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path of travel.
note: When ambulances, fire trucks, or police cars approach with lights or sirens, pull safely to the side and allow them to pass.

question: When interacting with pedestrians, what is required of drivers?
options: a:Yield only when pedestrians are legally entitled to cross.,b:Ensure the pedestrian is fully aware of your vehicle before proceeding.,c:Yield to pedestrians and do everything possible to avoid striking them, even if pedestrian is wrong.
note: Drivers must be alert to pedestrians and yield the right-of-way to avoid collisions, even if the pedestrian is crossing improperly.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Drive through shallow water at speed.,b:Drive more quickly to clear water.,c:Drive more slowly.
note: Hydroplaning occurs when tires lose traction on wet surfaces; reduce speed to lower the chance of hydroplaning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic signal changes from green to yellow as you approach, what is your best action?
options: a:Be prepared to stop safely rather than speed up to beat the light.,b:Speed up to beat the red light.,c:Stop abruptly in the center of the intersection.,d:Ignore it and continue at the same speed.
note: A steady yellow indicates the signal will soon turn red; prepare to stop if it is safe to do so.

question: Which factor commonly affects braking distance?
options: a:The speed your vehicle is traveling.,b:The condition of the pavement.,c:The condition of your brakes and tires.
note: Braking distance is affected by speed, vehicle condition (brakes and tires), and road surface conditions among other factors.

question: How do blind spots change with vehicle size?
options: a:Larger vehicles have larger blind spots.,b:Larger vehicles have smaller blind spots.,c:Larger vehicles have no blind spots.
note: The bigger the vehicle, the larger the blind spots. Trucks and SUVs have areas around them that drivers cannot see in mirrors.

question: Why is night driving typically more difficult than daytime driving?
options: a:Cars overheat more quickly at night.,b:Visibility is reduced in the dark.,c:It is more likely to rain at night.
note: At night your field of vision is reduced, so you must use proper headlights and reduce speed to be able to stop within visible distance.

question: If you are on a one-way street and an emergency vehicle using flashing lights approaches, what must you do?
options: a:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.,b:Turn on your hazard flashers and continue driving slowly.,c:Speed up and get out of the way by taking an exit.
note: On a one-way street, move to the nearest roadside and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass.

question: When must you pull over to the edge and allow an emergency vehicle to pass?
options: a:Regardless of the direction it is coming from.,b:Only if it is behind you.,c:Only if it is approaching from the opposite direction.
note: You must pull over to the right edge and stop for emergency vehicles with flashing lights or sirens regardless of whether they approach from behind or ahead.

question: What is the purpose of highway pavement markings?
options: a:They are usually not important.,b:They are only used in construction zones.,c:They provide important information for drivers.
note: Pavement markings inform drivers about lane usage, passing zones, and upcoming conditions to help position vehicles correctly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a stop is required at an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk, where should you stop?
options: a:You are not required to stop.,b:Slow down and check for crossing traffic.,c:Stop at the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can see traffic without entering it.
note: When no stop line or crosswalk is present, stop at the nearest point before the intersecting roadway that gives you a clear view of approaching traffic without entering the roadway.

question: What should you do on slippery roads to reduce the risk of collision?
options: a:Use alternate routes.,b:Drive the same as on dry roads.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: On slippery roads increase your following distance because it will take longer to stop safely under adverse conditions.

question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: Use low beam headlights (and fog lights if equipped) in fog. High beams reflect off fog and reduce visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do speed limit signs tell drivers?
options: a:Suggested speeds for the area.,b:The maximum or minimum legally allowed speed.,c:The speed to use in heavy traffic.
note: Speed limit signs indicate the legal maximum (and sometimes minimum) speed for ideal conditions; you must reduce speed when conditions require.

question: A flashing red traffic signal requires the same action as which sign?
options: a:A slow sign.,b:A yield sign.,c:A stop sign.
note: A flashing red signal has the same meaning as a stop sign: come to a complete stop, yield to traffic, then proceed when safe.

question: Which of the following is NOT a factor in stopping distance?
options: a:Steering ability.,b:Braking distance.,c:Reaction distance.
note: Stopping distance comprises perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance; steering skill is not a direct component though it affects overall control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What greatly increases stopping distances and crash severity?
options: a:High speeds.,b:Night drives only.,c:Slow speeds.,d:Daylight driving.
note: Driving at high speeds greatly increases stopping distance and the severity of a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your freeway exit, what should you do?
options: a:Make a U-turn across the median.,b:Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.,c:Continue to the next exit and leave there.
note: Do not stop, back up, or make illegal turns on a freeway; proceed to the next exit and safely return to your intended route.

question: When driving in fog, which headlights should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: Use low beams in fog, rain, or snow because high beams reflect back and reduce visibility.

question: Two solid yellow lines down the middle of the pavement mean:
options: a:Passing is allowed for drivers from both directions.,b:Passing is allowed under certain conditions.,c:Passing is not allowed from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate no passing from either direction; crossing is allowed only for permitted left turns.

question: If stopped by police, how should you behave?
options: a:Stay in your vehicle with hands visible on the wheel and wait for the officer to approach.,b:Unbuckle and get out immediately.,c:Retrieve paperwork while the officer is approaching.,d:Argue with the officer through the window.
note: Remain in your vehicle, keep hands visible, and wait for the officer's instructions; only retrieve documents when asked.

question: What does a red arrow signal on a traffic light require you to do?
options: a:Stop and remain stopped until a green light or green arrow appears.,b:Slow down and proceed if the way is clear.,c:Stop and then proceed when clear without waiting for green.
note: A red arrow requires a full stop and you must wait for a green signal or arrow before proceeding in that direction.

question: You may cross a dashed white line when:
options: a:Only during daylight hours.,b:At any time without checking for traffic.,c:It is safe to change lanes.
note: Broken white lines separate same-direction lanes and may be crossed for lane changes or passing when it is safe to do so.

question: Double solid yellow lines painted down the center of the road mean:
options: a:Railroad crossing ahead.,b:Pedestrian crossing ahead.,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow centerlines prohibit passing from both directions except to make a permitted left turn.

question: If you are in the right lane and intend to move into the left lane you should:
options: a:Look over your left shoulder to check the blind spot, and signal before changing lanes.,b:Only check mirrors and then change lanes.,c:Signal and immediately turn the wheel without looking.
note: Always check mirrors and glance over the shoulder toward the lane you intend to enter to ensure the blind spot is clear before signaling and moving.

question: In New Jersey, drivers under 21 are considered under the influence at which BAC level?
options: a:0.05 percent.,b:0.01 percent or higher.,c:0.10 percent.
note: New Jersey enforces a zero-tolerance law: drivers under 21 are subject to penalties with a BAC of 0.01% or higher.

question: If an approaching train is close enough to be a danger, what must you do?
options: a:Speed across the tracks quickly.,b:Proceed carefully while watching the train.,c:Cross at your own risk if no gates are down.,d:Not cross the tracks until the train has passed completely.
note: If a train is close enough to be hazardous, do not cross the tracks until it has fully passed and all warnings have stopped.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a 'No stopping' sign generally mean?
options: a:You may stop briefly to unload packages.,b:You may stop only to avoid a conflict with other traffic or to obey an officer or signal.,c:You may stop to discharge passengers.
note: A 'No stopping' sign means you may only stop to obey traffic laws, prevent a conflict with other vehicles, or follow directions from an officer or signal.

question: Before driving with snow and ice on your vehicle, which areas must be cleared?
options: a:All snow and ice from the entire vehicle, including the roof.,b:Only the vehicle's windows.,c:Only the hood of the vehicle.
note: State law requires removal of all snow and ice from your vehicle before driving to prevent hazards to you and others.

question: To change lanes safely you should:
options: a:Signal,b:Use turn indicator,c:Check mirrors and change lanes without signaling.
note: Always signal, check your mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving into another lane.

question: What should you do when it begins to rain while you are driving?
options: a:Drive faster than surrounding traffic.,b:Drive at the maximum posted speed.,c:Slow down.
note: When rain reduces visibility or traction, reduce your speed, turn on headlights, and if visibility becomes unsafe, pull off the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, where should you finish the turn?
options: a:In the left lane of the one-way street, closest to the lane you departed.,b:In the center of the street.,c:In the right lane of the street.
note: Complete the left turn into the lane nearest to the lane you came from on the one-way street.

question: If a transit vehicle signals to re-enter traffic after a stop, you must:
options: a:Yield to allow it to safely merge back into the main roadway.,b:Honk to let it know you're present.,c:Move only into the left lane.
note: Yield to transit vehicles signaling to re-enter the roadway after loading or unloading passengers by changing lanes, slowing, or stopping if necessary.
